radicals.meaning: ice, frost (written below)
radicals.story: Two short strokes hanging off the bottom of a character like a pair of icicles — the same ice mark as 冫, only written underneath instead of alongside.
radicals.variant_notes: 冫 is the left-hand form (冷, 次, 凝); ⺀ is the identical pair of strokes moved to the bottom (冬, 寒).
radicals.notes: Genuinely means ice in 冬 (winter) and 寒 (cold). In 図 it is a simplification artifact only.

radicals.meaning: An upright post with one tick jutting from its side.
radicals.story: A vertical post with a short mark sticking out to the right; in 上 it stands on the ground line 一 to show something is above.
radicals.variant_notes: The squared-off printing form of 卜; treat it as 卜 leaning into whatever sits below it.

radicals.meaning: Three short strokes standing up in a little tuft.
radicals.story: A short upright with one slanting mark on each side, like a tuft of hair sprouting from the top of 当.
radicals.variant_notes: The 小-derived top of 当/尚/常; keep it separate from the dotted 𭕄 top of 学/覚, which has no central upright.

radicals.meaning: A single stroke that rises to the right.
radicals.story: Just the pen-stroke itself: a short line starting low on the left and flicking up to the right, crossed by the hook 乚 to make 七.
radicals.notes: A stroke name, not a character; it exists only so 七 has two nameable halves.

radicals.meaning: no independent meaning; a single stroke that turns and sweeps to the lower left
radicals.story: One stroke that pushes right, snaps down and sweeps away to the lower left, like a small bird's beak turned down.
radicals.notes: It is the tick under the roof in 今 and the left-hand splash in 水.

radicals.meaning: no meaning of its own; two crossed strokes
radicals.story: Two strokes crossing to make an X — the shape of katakana メ, and in 気 a shorthand standing in for the 米 of the old form 氣.
radicals.notes: 乂 is its identical-looking twin in this dataset; both are just an X.

radicals.meaning: A baby being born head-first, with the birth waters streaming.
radicals.story: A child 子 drawn upside down with three streaks running out below it — a newborn arriving in a rush of water.
radicals.notes: The streaming water is why 流 means 'flow'.

radicals.meaning: A thick head of hair.
radicals.story: A person 人 with three sweeping strokes 彡 falling down behind them — a full mane of hair.
radicals.notes: Used only as the sound element of 珍 (チン); the same shape gives 診 シン.

radicals.meaning: all, every, the whole group
radicals.story: A roof 亼 over a bar 一 and two little people 从 — everybody gathered together under one cover.
radicals.variant_notes: 㑒 is the shinjitai reduction of 僉, and appears the same way in 検, 険 and 剣.
radicals.notes: Distinguish from 侖 (used in 倫/論), which also sits under a 亼 roof but has stacked bars beneath, not two people.

radicals.meaning: A boggy hollow where water collects.
radicals.story: A hollow 口 with two strokes 八 splitting open above it — water seeping down into the mud.
radicals.notes: The same element gives 沿 (エン); in 船 it is the sound beside the boat 舟.

radicals.meaning: two men standing side by side (a Japanese simplification)
radicals.story: Simply 夫 'husband' written twice, shoulder to shoulder; in the original 替 and 賛 this position held 兟 (two 先), which Japanese flattened into the easier double-夫 shape.
radicals.variant_notes: 𡗜 is the same double-夫 shape encoded separately; 兟 is the historical original (two 先) that this shape replaced in shinjitai.
radicals.notes: A pure shape — it carries no meaning of its own, so treat the pair of men purely as a mnemonic prop.

radicals.meaning: To get hold of something valuable.
radicals.story: A thumb 寸 pressed down on what was once a cowrie shell 貝, now flattened to 旦 — money in hand.
radicals.notes: 得 adds the going-man 彳: you go out and come back with the shell in your fist.

radicals.meaning: Two blades hacking; to wound, to cut down.
radicals.story: One halberd 戈 stacked directly on top of another — twice the blade, twice the damage.
radicals.variant_notes: The Japanese shape of 戔/戋 as written in 残, 浅, 銭.

radicals.meaning: No independent meaning; the head and front of the bear that 能 originally drew.
radicals.story: A hooked snout over a slab of flesh ⺝ — the front half of a bear, with the two 匕 on the right serving as its legs.
radicals.notes: 能 is widely explained as a bear pictograph (熊 later added the fire-legs); this element is the animal's front, not a meaning-bearing part on its own.

radicals.meaning: two marks over a bar; no independent meaning
radicals.story: A pair of short strokes perched on a horizontal bar like whiskers over a lip — modern print merged several unrelated older tops into it, so treat it as shape only.
radicals.notes: Distinguish from 丷 (horns), which is the same two marks without the bar, and from 亠 (lid), which is the bar without the marks.

radicals.meaning: The insect 虫 in the form it takes sealed inside 風.
radicals.story: An insect 虫 with one extra stroke ruled straight across the top of it, tucked inside the wind's frame.
radicals.variant_notes: Treat it as the same creature as 虫 — the only difference is the extra top stroke it grows when enclosed in 風.

radicals.meaning: the number one; as a component, a plain bar, the ground, or a lid line
radicals.story: A single horizontal stroke, the simplest mark a brush can make — and inside other characters it is usually just a bar: the ground under 上 and 下, the crossbar of 土.
radicals.notes: As a kanji it means one; as a component it almost never does — treat it as a line, a floor, or a ceiling depending on where it sits.

radicals.meaning: a nail or spike; a town block, the counter 丁
radicals.story: A nail seen from the side, flat head across the top and shaft hooking down — which is exactly what the hand in 打 (hit) is hammering.
radicals.notes: Sound carrier in 町 チョウ and 亭 テイ; in 可 it is a shape only.

radicals.meaning: no clear meaning of its own; traditionally 'breath meeting an obstruction', used mainly for sound
radicals.story: A flat bar with a leg that drops and hooks back to the left — the crook of a walking cane, which is exactly what the old man in 考 leans on.
radicals.notes: A reliable sound tag: 考 コウ, 号 ゴウ.

radicals.meaning: The number seven.
radicals.story: A rising stroke cut across by a hook — originally a notch scored through a line, borrowed early on for the number seven.

radicals.meaning: no meaning of its own; a flat top with a stroke sweeping down from its left end
radicals.story: Two strokes only: a flat bar with a stroke falling away from its left end, like the brim of a hat jutting out over whatever stands underneath.
radicals.notes: Same stroke family as 厂 (cliff), but its top bar extends past both sides; keep the two apart by image.

radicals.meaning: No; negation.
radicals.story: A ceiling bar 一 with a stem and two braces pushing up underneath and getting nowhere.
radicals.notes: Kept as the plain negator rather than a forced picture; the origin (a calyx? a bird rising?) is genuinely disputed.

radicals.meaning: To hand over, to grant, to bestow.
radicals.story: Two horizontal bars pinched around a hook in the middle, as if something were being passed across from one hand to another.

radicals.meaning: a stacked offering stand; the original form of 祖 (ancestor)
radicals.story: A tall stand with shelves stacked inside it and a foot at the base — the ancestral offering table that is the original of 祖.
radicals.notes: Chiefly a sound component: 阻 ソ, 粗 ソ, 組 ソ, 助 ジョ, 査 サ. 且 vs 旦: the stand rests on a baseline it overhangs, 旦 is a sun sitting on the horizon.

radicals.meaning: A generation; an era; the age one lives in.
radicals.story: Three tens 十 fused onto one baseline — thirty years, the span of a single generation.

radicals.meaning: No independent meaning here; an old way of writing 世.
radicals.story: Three short uprights pinned by a single crossbar — a stubby picket fence.
radicals.variant_notes: CJKVI matches the top of 帯 to the old form of 世, but that top is traditionally explained as ornaments hanging from a sash — so use it as a shape only.

radicals.meaning: The third of the ten calendar stems; no settled picture behind it.
radicals.story: A flat top with two splayed legs and a stem between them — it looks like a sawhorse, and since the real origin is disputed the shape is the safest hook.
radicals.notes: Purely the sound element inside the sickness frame 疒 in 病.

radicals.meaning: the toothed board a set of chime-bells hangs from (in 業); a bare shape in 並
radicals.story: Two uprights on a baseline with pegs sticking up — the toothed rack that ancient chime-bells hung from in 業, though in 並 the same printed shape is really just the feet of two people standing side by side.
radicals.notes: 業 'work, trade' descends from the craftsman who built that rack; 並 'line up' descends from the older 竝, two 立 side by side.

radicals.meaning: Two matching sides of one thing; both, a pair.
radicals.story: A single frame split down the middle with an identical hook hanging on each side — two matching halves inside one object.
radicals.variant_notes: Shinjitai squash of 兩.
radicals.notes: The standalone kanji keyword is 'both'; 'both halves' keeps the primitive imageable. Used only in 満.

radicals.meaning: To line up side by side; ordinary, average.
radicals.story: Two people standing (立) squashed shoulder to shoulder on a single ground line — a row.
radicals.variant_notes: Shinjitai squash of 竝, literally 立 + 立.
radicals.notes: Used only in 普 (the sun shining on a whole row — universal).

radicals.meaning: none — a bare vertical stroke with no meaning of its own
radicals.story: One straight vertical stroke top to bottom, a pole planted through the character; it means nothing by itself and only ever skewers or props up other shapes.
radicals.notes: Honest label: a shape. It is the line through the box in 中, the bowstring in 引, the stem in 半 — never a meaning.

radicals.meaning: Two strands twisted around each other.
radicals.story: Two lines wound together into a single knot, like a tie twisted shut — in 収 a hand 又 grabs it and gathers it in.

radicals.meaning: plank bed, couch (left-hand form of 爿)
radicals.story: The left half of a tree (木) split down the grain and stood on end — a plank bed, which is exactly what 寝 (sleep) needs.
radicals.variant_notes: 爿 is the full traditional form; 丬 is the abbreviated left-hand column used throughout Japanese printing (状, 将, 寝).
radicals.notes: 爿 and 片 are the two halves of a split 木, mirror images of each other — 丬 opens to the right, 片 to the left. 疒 (sickbed) is this same bed tipped on its side.

radicals.meaning: A shaft crossed by three bars.
radicals.story: One upright skewers three horizontals — the head of a garden rake.
radicals.variant_notes: In 拝 this element is really the second hand 手 pressed together in prayer, drawn with an extra crossbar.

radicals.meaning: a single dot or tick
radicals.story: One teardrop-shaped tick — a single falling drop of ink or water.
radicals.notes: In 太, 玉 and 犬 the droplet is a distinguishing mark tacked onto a bigger character, not a real drop.

radicals.meaning: none of its own — the top-of-character form of 八
radicals.story: Two short strokes leaning away from each other like a pair of little horns; it is 八 written at the top of a character and carries no meaning by itself.
radicals.variant_notes: 八 splays downward and outward at the bottom of a character; 丷 leans outward at the top (半, 平, 弟, 金, 商, 楽). Same two strokes, opposite posture.
radicals.notes: Not a Kangxi radical. Identical to katakana ソ in some fonts. Honest label: a shape — do not let a story claim it means 'eight' in 立 or 商.

radicals.meaning: Round; a pellet or ball.
radicals.story: A curled stroke wrapped around a single dot — something rolled up round.
radicals.notes: In 執 this 丸 is a worn-down form of an older element showing a kneeling person with arms outstretched; the modern shape is plain 丸, so compose with 'ball'.

radicals.meaning: master, owner, lord; main, principal
radicals.story: A lamp stand with the flame (丶) burning on top — the household light, and by extension the one who owns the house.
radicals.notes: Indexed under Kangxi radical 3 (丶). 主 vs 玉: 主's dot sits ON TOP of the king; 玉's sits inside at the lower right. Sound-wise it hands チュウ to 注 and 柱 but 住 breaks rank at ジュウ.

radicals.meaning: none — a bare diagonal stroke with no meaning of its own
radicals.story: One stroke sweeping down and to the left like a blade-cut; it carries no meaning at all and only ever shows up as a piece of something bigger.
radicals.notes: Honest label: this is a shape, not a meaning. Use it as decoration in stories (a scar, a swipe, a sword-cut) rather than pretending it signifies anything.

radicals.meaning: a falling right-hand brush stroke; no independent meaning
radicals.story: The single stroke that falls away toward the lower right, starting thin and widening into a flick — the mirror image of 丿, and pure calligraphy with no meaning of its own.
radicals.notes: Shows up only where a character has to be broken all the way down to strokes (水, 長, 展). Pairs with 丿 (the leftward slash) to make the splayed legs of a glyph.

radicals.meaning: to mow, to cut down; as a component, simply two crossing strokes
radicals.story: Two strokes crossing like a blade sweeping through a stalk — on its own the character means 'to mow', but inside 文, 父, 図 and 更 it is only a crossing of strokes with no meaning.
radicals.notes: Distinct from 㐅 (the X inside 気 and 希), which is written as a symmetrical cross rather than a slash cut by a rising stroke.

radicals.meaning: A long stretch of time; longevity.
radicals.story: The strokes read as a person 人 with an extra bar laid across their back, pinned in place so long they never get away.
radicals.notes: The graphic origin is disputed; the person-held-back reading is a shape reading, not settled scholarship.

radicals.meaning: A young plant whose one leaf droops over.
radicals.story: A slash cuts across an upright that hooks at the foot — a thin stalk with a single leaf flopping off the side.

radicals.meaning: abruptly, suddenly; the original form of 作 (to make)
radicals.story: The origin is disputed, so read the shape as it stands: a board with two notches cut across it and a stroke slicing down its left side.
radicals.notes: Because it is the parent of 作, both 作 and 昨 read サク.

radicals.meaning: A shape of sound flaring outward.
radicals.story: Two flare-marks over a bar on a hooked stem — read it as a horn with the noise spraying out of its bell.

radicals.meaning: To get up on top of something and ride it.
radicals.story: A figure standing high with feet planted across the branches — the old form 乘 drew a person 大 up in a tree 木.

radicals.meaning: a hook stroke that drops and flicks up; the compressed form of 乙
radicals.story: A line that drops straight down and then flicks up at the end — the barbed tip of a fishhook.
radicals.variant_notes: 乙 is the full standalone form; 乚 is the squeezed hook used as a final stroke inside characters (七, 札, 礼, 電).
radicals.notes: Pure stroke-shape — it carries no meaning in the characters that use it.

radicals.meaning: A horizontal stroke whose right end turns down.
radicals.story: Picture a small awning: a flat top edge that bends down at the right corner, the roof over the hook of 了.

radicals.meaning: nine
radicals.story: A single hooked stroke curling back on itself and nearly closing the circle — one short of ten.
radicals.notes: Indexed under Kangxi radical 5 (乙), not a radical itself. In 究 it is the キュウ sound; in 雑 it is a simplification artifact with no meaning.

radicals.meaning: a curling body with a raised tail; (classical) 'namely, indeed'
radicals.story: A curling body with a tail whipping up on the right — read it as a scorpion with its stinger raised, since the true origin is disputed.
radicals.notes: Clean チ phonetic in 地 and 池; 他 breaks the pattern and takes タ. Never appears anywhere but the right side.

radicals.meaning: a hooked vertical stroke; no independent meaning
radicals.story: One vertical stroke with a small hook flicking to the left at its foot — a barb or gaff point, never written alone.
radicals.notes: A Kangxi radical that is purely a stroke. Keep it distinct from 丨 (no hook), 乚 (hooks upward at the end of a bend) and 𠃌 (turns the corner from a horizontal).

radicals.meaning: beforehand, in advance
radicals.story: Its origin is disputed — often read as a weaver's shuttle passed forward through the threads — so simply see a small hook (龴) set above a longer hook, one thing readied before the next.
radicals.notes: Shares its top 龴 with 矛 'spear'; 矛 adds a slash and an extra stroke.

radicals.meaning: The standard of office, hence official business.
radicals.story: A hand grips a tall shaft that runs the full height of the character, a boxed emblem hoisted near its top.
radicals.notes: Same family as 史 and 吏 — a hand holding an official's standard — which is why 事 came to mean 'matter, affair'.

radicals.meaning: two, the number 2
radicals.story: Two horizontal strokes stacked with the lower one longer — a tally of two.
radicals.notes: Really the number two only in 三. In 夫, 半, 用 and 発 the pair of horizontals is a stroke collision, not a count.

radicals.meaning: the right half of a crossroads; no independent meaning
radicals.story: The right-hand half of 行, which is the old picture of a four-way crossroads, so this is literally the far lane of the street.
radicals.notes: Never written alone. 彳 + 亍 = 行 (go); in 街, 術 and 衝 the two lanes straddle whatever is walking down the middle of the road.

radicals.meaning: A bar over a stem that kinks and hooks.
radicals.story: A flat top with a stem bending at the elbow beneath it, like a length of pipe with a crook in it; this is the old 于 written flat.

radicals.meaning: rising vapor; (classical) to say
radicals.story: Two flat strokes with a curl coiling beneath them — rising vapor, the original picture of a cloud before 雨 was stacked on top to make 雲.
radicals.notes: Typed 'shape' honestly: in 会, 伝 and 転 it is a post-war stand-in for quite different traditional components (會, 傳, 轉), not a cloud. 云 vs 去: 去 has 土 on top, 云 has 二.

radicals.meaning: The timber frame built around a well mouth.
radicals.story: Two uprights crossed by two horizontals — the wooden crib laid around the top of a well shaft.

radicals.meaning: The cross-shaped floor plan of an ancient tomb; also 'Asia' in modern use.
radicals.story: A symmetrical frame notched in on all four sides — the plan of a royal burial chamber seen from above.
radicals.variant_notes: 亜 is the shinjitai of 亞.
radicals.notes: 悪 sets a heart 心 down inside the tomb chamber.

radicals.meaning: Pressed to the utmost; urgent, extreme.
radicals.story: A figure with a mouth (口) and a hand (又) wedged between a ceiling stroke and a floor stroke — squeezed to the absolute limit.
radicals.notes: Used only in 極.

radicals.meaning: none of its own — a decorative top piece, read as a lid or cap
radicals.story: A single dot resting on a horizontal bar — a pot lid with its little knob on top.
radicals.notes: Honest label: this is a shape. It has no meaning in 六, 文, 方, 市 — it is just the hat those characters wear.

radicals.meaning: perish, die, be lost; flee, disappear
radicals.story: A person bent double behind a screen (乚) — someone who has fled and is now gone, a sense that slid from 'vanish' into 'perish, die'.
radicals.notes: Often glossed 'deceased'; 'fugitive' is used because 'gone/fled' is what actually powers the derivatives — 忘 the memory that fled the heart, 忙 the heart gone missing, 望 gazing after someone who has gone. Perfectly regular ボウ phonetic across all three.

radicals.meaning: cross, intersect, mix, exchange, socialize
radicals.story: A standing person — head (亠) and arms (八) on top — with the two bottom strokes scissored over each other like crossed legs.
radicals.notes: Heisig's keyword is 'mingle'; the crossed-legs image is the same character.

radicals.meaning: the two points under a person's arms; later borrowed to write 'also'
radicals.story: A person seen head-on with a mark dotted under each arm — this was the original way of writing 'armpit' before the character was borrowed for 'also'.
radicals.notes: In 変 'change' and 恋 'love' it is only a postwar simplification of the older 䜌 (tangled threads), so it contributes neither sound nor sense there — read it as a shape.

radicals.meaning: No independent meaning; the trimmed top of 彦, used for its sound.
radicals.story: A standing figure 立 with a stroke slashing away to the left, as if leaning over.
radicals.notes: 産 is this shape wrapped over 生 'life'; the top is a phonetic reduction, so do not read a picture into it.

radicals.meaning: capital city
radicals.story: A pictograph of a tall ceremonial building raised on a mound: a roof-lid (亠) over the gatehouse (口), standing on splayed pillars (小).
radicals.notes: The same tall-building pictograph as the top of 高; 京 is the shorter, un-storeyed version.

radicals.meaning: a tree standing tall (the shared element of 新 and 親)
radicals.story: In modern Japanese it is simply 立 'stand' set on 木 'tree' — a tree standing upright — though the top was originally 辛, a tattooing needle.
radicals.notes: The classic Japanese memory aid for 親 reads the parts literally: 木の上に立って見る — standing on a tree to watch over the children.

radicals.meaning: person, human being, people
radicals.story: Two legs meeting at the top, one longer than the other — a person striding, seen from the side.
radicals.variant_notes: 人 stands alone or sits at the bottom; 亻 is the left-side form (仕, 代, 任); 𠆢 is the flattened top form that roofs 今, 会, 全.
radicals.notes: 入 (enter) crosses at the top with the short stroke on the LEFT; 人 has the strokes meeting cleanly at the apex; 八 never touches at all.

radicals.meaning: a human being, standing upright at the side of the character
radicals.story: A person 人 turned sideways and flattened against the left wall: the short stroke is the head and shoulder, the long one the body and trailing leg.
radicals.variant_notes: 人 stands alone or sits at the bottom; 亻 (にんべん) is the left-side form; 𠆢 is the roof-like top form (今, 会, 全).
radicals.notes: Parent is 人. 亻 is two strokes, 彳 (sidewalk) is three — that extra flick is the whole difference.

radicals.meaning: a peaked cover over a bar; no independent meaning
radicals.story: A peaked cover set down on a single bar — a pup tent, or a lid dropping onto a pot as it does in 合 (fit together).
radicals.notes: Only ever the cap of a character (今, 合, 余). Distinguish from bare 人/𠆢, which has no bar underneath — 茶 uses 人, not 亼.

radicals.meaning: The present moment.
radicals.story: A roof-like 亼 clapped down over a small hook, sealing this instant off from everything that came before.

radicals.meaning: To come between, to mediate; originally a man in scale armor.
radicals.story: A person 人 with a plate hung on either side of the body — a man buckled into armor, standing between you and the blow.
radicals.notes: In 界 it gives both the sound カイ and the sense of 'coming between' that a boundary implies.

radicals.meaning: Something attached, stuck on, or handed over.
radicals.story: A hand 寸 reaching up and pressing against a person 亻 — whatever it touches, it sticks to.

radicals.meaning: A stand-in; a generation, an era, a fee paid in place of something.
radicals.story: A person (亻) planted beside a staked marker (弋) — a stand-in holding someone else's place.
radicals.notes: Used only in 貸 (money handed over as a substitute — lending).

radicals.meaning: command, order, decree
radicals.story: A canopy (亼) with a person kneeling beneath it (卩) — a subject down on one knee taking the boss's command.
radicals.notes: 令 has the kneeling 卩 under the roof; 今 has only a short tick and bar.

radicals.meaning: by means of, using; from (a given point)
radicals.story: The right half is a person (人) and the left an old hand-plow with its blade — the origin is disputed, so simply picture someone holding the tool they get the job done by means of.
radicals.notes: The kanji itself is grammatical (以上, 以来); the plow is only the memory image.

radicals.meaning: To hand a load over to someone; duty, appointment.
radicals.story: A person (亻) beside 壬, a spindle bulging in the middle with its load — the burden handed over for someone to carry.
radicals.notes: Used only in 賃 (money for a job entrusted — wages, rent).

radicals.meaning: People coming together; a gathering.
radicals.story: A peaked lid (𠆢) clapped over 云 — everyone gathered under one roof.
radicals.variant_notes: Shinjitai squash of 會.
radicals.notes: Used only in 絵 (threads meeting each other — embroidery, hence picture).

radicals.meaning: What, how many (as a kanji); a man shouldering a load (the original picture).
radicals.story: A person 亻 beside 可, drawn originally as a man with a burden hoisted onto his shoulder.
radicals.notes: As a flashcard 何 means 'what'; as a building block keep the porter image — it is exactly why 荷 (grass + porter) means luggage.

radicals.meaning: What is left over; excess, remainder.
radicals.story: A peaked roof (𠆢) set on a propped post (朩) — originally a lean-to shed, best read as the storehouse where everything left over gets stacked.
radicals.notes: Used only in 塗 (leftover slurry of water and soil, slapped on as plaster).

radicals.meaning: bound writing-slips gathered under a lid in strict order
radicals.story: A lid (亼) closed over a stack of bamboo writing-slips (冊), which are useless unless they are threaded in the right order.
radicals.notes: 論 'argue, treatise' is words put in that order; 倫 'ethics' is people put in it.

radicals.meaning: to hollow a log into a boat; assent, yes
radicals.story: A pointed prow 亼 over a hull 月 with the blade-strokes 刂 that scooped it out — a log hollowed into a canoe.
radicals.variant_notes: 兪 is the older printed form; 俞 is the shape inside 輸.
radicals.notes: Kept as 'dugout canoe' so it never blurs with 舟 'boat'; cart 車 + dugout canoe gives 輸 'transport' cleanly.

radicals.meaning: human legs; a person seen from the waist down
radicals.story: Two bare legs, one planted and one striding away — what is left of a person 人 once something else has taken over the top of the character.
radicals.notes: Always at the bottom, always a person: 兄, 先, 児, 見, 売, 発. 几 (table) has a flat top bar connecting its two strokes; 儿 does not.

radicals.meaning: A flat top carried on two legs.
radicals.story: One bar 一 laid straight across the legs 儿 — a stool you could sit on.

radicals.meaning: elder brother, the senior male of the family
radicals.story: A big mouth (口) mounted on a pair of legs (儿) — the family member who does the talking and hands out orders.
radicals.notes: 祝 'celebrate' shows him at an altar (礻) reciting the blessing; 況 takes only the キョウ sound.

radicals.meaning: To fill out, be full, allot.
radicals.story: An upside-down child (𠫓, head-first out of the womb) standing on a pair of legs (儿) — a baby grown out and filled in to full size.
radicals.notes: Used only in 統 (threads gathered and packed into one skein).

radicals.meaning: The one who got there first; ahead, previous.
radicals.story: A foot striding out above a pair of human legs 儿 — someone already out in front of everybody else.

radicals.meaning: to slip out, get let off, be exempted
radicals.story: A pair of legs (儿) wriggling out from under a heavy headdress — and the whole shape is 兎 'rabbit' minus its tail-dot, exactly the rabbit that got away.
radicals.notes: 晩 'evening' is the sun making its escape below the horizon; 勉 'exertion' is the power it takes to get out.

radicals.meaning: to speak with pleasure; delighted
radicals.story: A person (儿) with a wide-open mouth (口) and two little puffs of breath escaping above it — a face breaking into a grin as it talks.
radicals.variant_notes: 兌 spreads the top strokes outward as 八; Japanese printing uses 兑, with the two short strokes 丷 leaning inward. Same element either way.
radicals.notes: The 'delight' sense survives in 悦; in 税 and 説 it is mostly the sound ゼイ/セツ.

radicals.meaning: enter, go in, insert
radicals.story: Two strokes meeting at a peak and opening downward like the mouth of a cave — the shape draws you in under it.
radicals.notes: 入 has one stroke starting higher and crossing over the other; 人's two strokes meet flush at the top.

radicals.meaning: eight; and, in many characters, the act of splitting one thing into two
radicals.story: Two strokes falling apart as they descend, never touching — the number eight, and equally the picture of something being divided.
radicals.variant_notes: 丷 is the top-of-character form, written with the strokes leaning outward instead of splaying downward (半, 平, 弟).
radicals.notes: Carries real meaning ('split') in 分, 公, 半; elsewhere (六, 火, 父, 共, 具) it is just two legs or a pair of hands at the bottom. Unlike 人 and 入, its strokes never meet.

radicals.meaning: jointly, in common, shared by both
radicals.story: Two hands (the 八 underneath) raising a single load between them, because nobody can lift it alone.
radicals.notes: 供 'offer, accompany' adds the person doing the presenting; the top half alone is the separate shape 龷.

radicals.meaning: two hands lifting a burning torch (in 送); a shinjitai stand-in elsewhere
radicals.story: Two sparks (丷) flying off the top of what looks like 天 — in 送 'see off' this really is a pair of hands lifting a torch to light a traveller out, while in 関 the same printed shape merely stands in for the old gate bolt.
radicals.notes: Because its two uses have different origins, treat it as one shape with one image and let the story do the work.

radicals.meaning: several hands raising something together — the postwar squash of 與
radicals.story: All that survives of 與, four hands passing a load up between them — the ticks are the fingers and the bar is the thing being lifted.
radicals.notes: 挙 'raise' adds the hand (手) doing it; 誉 'honor' is praise lifted up in words (言). Do not confuse with the three-spark cap 𭕄 of 学, 栄 and 単.

radicals.meaning: Soldier, troops, arms.
radicals.story: An axe 斤 gripped in two hands 廾 — the armed man.
radicals.notes: 浜 is the shortened form of 濱; 兵 stands in for the older sound element 賓 and carries no 'soldier' sense there. Distinguish from 戒, which is a halberd rather than an axe in two hands.

radicals.meaning: a wide woven tray for tossing grain, set on a stand
radicals.story: A cross-hatched woven tray sitting on a two-legged stand (八) — the winnowing basket farmers toss grain in, and the original of 箕.
radicals.notes: 基 'foundation' is that basket set down on the soil; 期 'period, term' borrows only the キ sound. As a word 其 was long ago borrowed to mean 'that'.

radicals.meaning: Tool, equipment, the gear you have on hand.
radicals.story: A vessel held up on a pair of propping hands 八 — the kit you keep ready.
radicals.notes: 真 splits into 十 + 具 by modern shape only; historically its lower half is a corrupted cauldron, so compose the mnemonic from the shapes rather than claiming an origin.

radicals.meaning: to hold two things at once, concurrently
radicals.story: One hand gripping two grain stalks at the same time — the doubled uprights are the stalks, the strokes crossing them the fist.
radicals.notes: Tucked inside 广 in 廉, on the right in 謙. Purely a sound-carrier in both.

radicals.meaning: an open-bottomed frame; the 'upside-down box' enclosure
radicals.story: A flat roof carried on two posts and open along the bottom — a shop awning you can walk in under.
radicals.notes: Open at the bottom, unlike 囗 which is sealed on all four sides.

radicals.meaning: Japanese yen; round, a circle.
radicals.story: A box 冂 with a bar and an upright inside — the round coin of the old form 圓 squared off into modern shorthand.

radicals.meaning: No independent meaning; the lower storey of 高.
radicals.story: A frame 冂 with a small opening 口 inside it — the ground floor of a tall building.
radicals.notes: 高 stacks a roof 亠 and an upper window 口 on top of this base to make a tower.

radicals.meaning: A bright window (the sense of this old character).
radicals.story: A frame 冂 with slats set inside it, letting the light through.
radicals.variant_notes: 囧 is the same window written with the slats splayed.
radicals.notes: CJKVI matches the bottom of 商 to this shape; 商's own origin is disputed, so use it as a shape and do not build an etymology on it.

radicals.meaning: to interlock, to build up in layers
radicals.story: Two matching halves notched together, one stacked squarely on the other — a joinery diagram, which is why it builds 構 'structure' and 講 'lecture'.
radicals.notes: A rock-solid コウ series: 構, 講, 溝, 購.

radicals.meaning: a cover thrown over something; a lid, cap, or covering cloth
radicals.story: A flat lid with a small tab dropping at the left corner — originally a cloth thrown over an object, easiest to picture as a plain crown resting on whatever is below.
radicals.notes: Called わかんむり. 宀 (roof) is the same shape with a dot on top. In 学, 覚, 労 this 冖 is not really a cover — it is what a larger top element collapsed into.

radicals.meaning: ice, frozen water
radicals.story: Two crisp ticks where the three strokes of 氵 have frozen down and shrunk — water gone solid.
radicals.notes: Two ticks, not three — that is the whole difference from water 氵. Real ice in 冷 and 凝; in 次, 弱 and 然 the two ticks come from elsewhere.

radicals.meaning: Winter; originally the end of the year.
radicals.story: Two trailing ends hanging down with a pair of ice drops ⺀ frozen beneath them — the tail end of the year.
radicals.notes: 冬 was the original way to write 'end'; 終 added the thread 糸 to specify the end of a cord.

radicals.meaning: a low table or bench
radicals.story: Two strokes making a low bench: a flat top with a leg bending down at each end.
radicals.notes: In 風 the frame is really a squeezed 凡 (a sail) doing sound duty, not a table.

radicals.meaning: a pit, hollow, open-topped container
radicals.story: Three strokes walling off a space that is open at the top — a pit dug into the ground, which is exactly what a sprout is climbing out of in 出.
radicals.notes: Also commonly glossed 'open box' or 'receptacle'; 'pit' is used here so it stays distinct from 囗 (enclosure), 匚 (box) and 口 (mouth), and because the pit makes 出 (exit) obvious.

radicals.meaning: sword, single-edged blade, knife
radicals.story: A curved single-edged blade with a stub of handle at the top — a sword drawn in two strokes.
radicals.variant_notes: 刀 is the full form, used standing alone or at the bottom/inside a character; 刂 is the narrow form used on the right.
radicals.notes: 刀 vs 力: the sword's first stroke turns down at the corner, the muscle 力 pushes a slash out to the left.

radicals.meaning: knife, sword; the right-hand form of 刀
radicals.story: The sword 刀 stood upright and squeezed flat against the right edge, its handle gone and only the straight cutting edge left.
radicals.variant_notes: 刀 stands alone or sits at the bottom/inside (分, 券, 解); 刂 is the two-stroke form used only on the right (判, 別, 割).
radicals.notes: Parent form is 刀. If it is on the right and it cuts, it is 刂.

radicals.meaning: A hand curling shut on something.
radicals.story: A bent stroke closes down over the hand-shape ヨ, fingers curling to seize — in 急 it is what remains of 及, a hand catching someone from behind.

radicals.meaning: Punishment: the restraining frame and the blade.
radicals.story: Two uprights crossed by two bars 开 make a set of wooden stocks, with the sword 刂 waiting alongside.

radicals.meaning: A crescent slab set beside a knife.
radicals.story: The flesh-moon ⺝ standing next to the sword 刂 — read the pair as one curved, moon-shaped blade.
radicals.variant_notes: Inside 前 the ⺝ is really a squashed boat 舟, and the whole character once meant a foot advancing on a boat.

radicals.meaning: a line of things laid out in order; to arrange in a file
radicals.story: Stripped bones (歹) being taken apart with a knife (刂) and laid out one beside the next.
radicals.notes: 例 'example' is one person pulled out of the row to stand for the rest; 裂 'split' keeps the cutting sense, tearing cloth (衣).

radicals.meaning: To cut into shape; regulate, control, system.
radicals.story: A knife (刂) trimming back a branching tree — cutting things down to regulation shape.
radicals.notes: Used only in 製 (cloth 衣 cut to a controlled pattern — manufacture).

radicals.meaning: Rule, law, norm.
radicals.story: A knife 刂 carving alongside what was once a bronze cauldron (now flattened to 貝) — the law cut where everyone can read it.

radicals.meaning: power, strength, force, effort
radicals.story: A stroke hooked at the shoulder that swells and drives down — an arm flexing its bicep (the ancient origin is disputed and may be a plow rather than a limb).
radicals.notes: Sits on the right (功, 加, 助) or the bottom (努, 労, 男). 刀 (sword) has its hook on the LEFT stroke; 力's long stroke pushes down past the hook.

radicals.meaning: To add on, to pile up, to increase.
radicals.story: A flexed arm 力 set beside a mouth 口 — muscle and words heaped one on top of the other.

radicals.meaning: the strength of several arms pulling at once
radicals.story: Three copies of 力 'power' stacked in a pyramid — three arms straining on the same rope.
radicals.notes: 協 'cooperate' adds ten (十) more hands to the three; 脅 'threaten' is three powers bearing down on your body (⺝).

radicals.meaning: To labour until worn out.
radicals.story: Two hands rolling something above a straining arm 力 — hard, wearing work.
radicals.notes: Modern 勝 splits by shape into 月 + 劵; historically it is 力 'strength' with 朕 as the sound element, so this entry exists to name the shape, not to explain 勝's origin.

radicals.meaning: To move, set in motion.
radicals.story: Something heavy (重) with muscle (力) put behind it — shifting a load.
radicals.notes: Used only in 働, a Japanese-made kanji: a person doing the moving, i.e. working.

radicals.meaning: to wrap, to fold around, to enclose
radicals.story: A person bending double, the arm curving right over and hooking back to fold something up inside it.
radicals.notes: Always wraps whatever sits beneath it: 句 wraps a mouth, 包 wraps a baby, 勺 wraps a drop.

radicals.meaning: a long-handled dipper with something in its bowl
radicals.story: A wrapping stroke (勹) curled around a single drop — a dipper with one spoonful still sitting in the bowl.
radicals.notes: 的 'target' is the white spot you ladle your aim onto; 約 'promise' is a thread tied off to an agreed measure. Distinct from 匕 'spoon' and 斗 'dipper' (the big grain scoop).

radicals.meaning: A pole with cloth ribbons trailing off it.
radicals.story: A bent pole 勹 with three slanting ribbons streaming from its side, like a signal flag snapping in the wind.

radicals.meaning: a ladle or spoon; by extension a person bent or turned around
radicals.story: A shallow bowl on a bent handle, tipped as if pouring.
radicals.notes: 匕 vs 七: the spoon's slash starts above and cuts down through the hook; in 七 the horizontal bar crosses a vertical hook. In 化 and 北 the 匕 is really a person drawn flipped or facing away, which is why they mean 'change' and 'back/north'.

radicals.meaning: One thing turning into another.
radicals.story: A standing person 亻 beside the same person tipped upside down 匕 — the moment of transformation caught in a single frame.

radicals.meaning: North; originally the back of the body.
radicals.story: Two people standing back to back — the original picture of 'back', later borrowed for the cold direction you turn your back on.
radicals.notes: In 背 it does double duty: it supplies the sound and its own original 'back' sense, with flesh ⺝ added underneath to put the back on a body.

radicals.meaning: a right-opening container; box, receptacle
radicals.story: Two strokes bent into a box with the right-hand side left open — a container lying on its side, mouth facing you, ready to have something shoved in (医 shoves an arrow in).
radicals.notes: Heisig calls it simply 'box'; 'open box' keeps the missing right wall in view, which is the whole point. 匸 (hiding) is a different radical with a flat lid.

radicals.meaning: ten, complete set; also a plain cross or crossing point
radicals.story: One horizontal crossed by one vertical at the middle — ten fingers counted off by crossing both hands at the wrists.
radicals.notes: Lends ジュウ in 汁. Heisig calls this primitive 'needle' — either image works, but keep to one. 千 is 十 with a slash on top; 干 has a second horizontal.

radicals.meaning: No independent meaning; a variant way of writing 'twenty'.
radicals.story: Two short uprights joined by a single crossbar.
radicals.variant_notes: A variant of 廿 'twenty', but in 備 it is not a number at all — it is the top of the old quiver pictograph, so treat it strictly as shape.

radicals.meaning: Nine over ten; the squeezed abbreviation of 卒.
radicals.story: Literally nine 九 stacked on ten 十 — a shorthand block that survives in the Japan-made character 枠.

radicals.meaning: A ladle-sized measure for grain or sake.
radicals.story: A scoop with its handle jutting out to the side and one mark on the bowl showing how full it is.

radicals.meaning: Midday; the Horse, seventh of the earthly branches.
radicals.story: A shaft with a thickened head — originally a pestle, later borrowed for the hour of the Horse at midday.
radicals.notes: 許 belongs to the 午 sound series even though its reading came out as キョ.

radicals.meaning: One half.
radicals.story: An ox 牛 with the splitting mark 丷 sitting on its back — the animal divided straight down the middle.

radicals.meaning: (as a shape) a dancer's hanging plumes; as a character, the tally numeral forty
radicals.story: Long plumes hanging from a crossbar — the ornaments a shaman held in both hands while dancing, which is what 無 and 舞 both originally drew; standing alone the character is just the tally 'forty'.
radicals.notes: Inside 無 and 舞 it is drawn as a lattice with an extra bar above it; 卅 is thirty, 廿 is twenty.

radicals.meaning: Single, one alone; simple.
radicals.story: Two horns (丷) on a boxed 田 with a single stake driven straight through — the old 單, a one-piece forked hunting weapon.
radicals.variant_notes: Shinjitai of 單.
radicals.notes: Used only in 戦 (single combat with halberds — war).

radicals.meaning: divination, fortune-telling
radicals.story: A straight rod with a tick branching off its side, echoing the forked crack that opened in a heated oracle bone and was read as an omen.
radicals.notes: In 下 it is really just a mark set below the line, not divination; ⺊ (top of 上) is its mirror image.

radicals.meaning: divine, tell fortunes; occupy, hold
radicals.story: The crack in a heated turtle shell (卜) sitting above the mouth (口) that reads it aloud — the diviner calling out the omen.
radicals.notes: Strong テン phonetic (店, 点). The second meaning 'occupy' (占める) is what 独占 'monopoly' uses; the fortune-teller image only serves the writing, not that sense.

radicals.meaning: a kneeling figure; a split tally or seal
radicals.story: A person seen from the side with the knees folded under — the vertical is the back, the little hook the tucked-up leg.
radicals.variant_notes: 㔾 is the same kneeling figure squashed beneath a kanji (危, 巻); 卩 is the upright form standing on the right-hand side (印, 即, 却).
radicals.notes: In 印 a hand (爫) presses down on this kneeling figure — which is how the character came to mean 'stamp a seal'.

radicals.meaning: One who kneels and gazes up at another.
radicals.story: A standing figure on the left leaning over a kneeling one 卩 on the right, the kneeler's face tilted upward.

radicals.meaning: Drawn right up to the food; hence 'at once, on the spot'.
radicals.story: A heaped food bowl (皀) with a person kneeling at it (卩) — pulled straight up to the dish without a moment's delay.
radicals.notes: 卩 on its own is the bare kneeling figure; this compound adds the bowl. Used only in 節.

radicals.meaning: a cliff, a rock overhang
radicals.story: A flat overhang with one wall dropping away beneath it — a rock face you can shelter under.
radicals.notes: 厂 vs 广: 广 is the same cliff with a dot on top — a roof built against it, so it means a building. Bare 厂 is raw rock.

radicals.meaning: A grindstone; the abbreviated 厲.
radicals.story: Under a cliff 厂 sits 万 — the rough slab quarried out of the cliff face and used for sharpening blades.

radicals.meaning: open plain, field; source, origin, original
radicals.story: A spring welling out from under a cliff 厂 — the source of the stream and the broad grassy plain it waters.
radicals.notes: One of the 811. Heisig's established 'meadow' is kept because 'field' would collide with 田 and 'plain' is ambiguous; the card's 'original/source' sense is the spring at the foot of the cliff. 願 uses it for the ゲン→ガン sound.

radicals.meaning: none reliably — a catch-all shape; in a few characters it preserves an old sense of 'private, oneself'
radicals.story: A small hook curling back on itself, exactly the shape of katakana ム — picture an elbow tucked in to hide something, but know that this glyph is honestly a simplification of several unrelated old elements.
radicals.notes: Be honest with learners: in 私 and 公 it descends from an old 'private/self' sign, but in 仏, 台, 広, 参 it is just what a bigger element got squashed into. Use the elbow image consistently anyway.

radicals.meaning: To leave, to depart; the past.
radicals.story: A figure stepping up and out of the little enclosure 厶 beneath — walking off the premises.

radicals.meaning: hand; grabbing, taking, doing — the hand that reaches in
radicals.story: Two strokes for a wrist with its fingers folded down — the right hand, drawn as the one that reaches out and takes hold.
radicals.notes: Look for the grabbing: 取 (grab an ear), 受 (receive), 友 (two hands clasped), 反 (a hand against a cliff). 夂 adds a short stroke on top and sits high in the character.

radicals.meaning: To reach, to catch up with, to extend as far as.
radicals.story: A hand 又 closing on the heel of the person 人 running ahead — caught at last.

radicals.meaning: turn over, reverse, warp back; anti-, oppose
radicals.story: A hand (又) tucked under a cliff overhang (厂) with the palm turning upward — the gesture of flipping something over, which slid into reversing and opposing.
radicals.notes: Keyword is 'flip' rather than Heisig's 'anti' because flipping reads cleanly in every derivative: 板 a flipped plank, 飯 rice turned in the pot, 返 turn back, 坂 a slope that flips you over.

radicals.meaning: Father's younger brother.
radicals.story: A hand (又) reaching past a stalk with beans scattering off it (⺊ + 小) — the picture was borrowed to write 'uncle'.
radicals.notes: Used only in 督 (the uncle's eye 目 kept on you — supervision).

radicals.meaning: take, seize, obtain
radicals.story: A hand (又) closing on an ear (耳) — ancient soldiers cut an ear from each fallen enemy to count what they had taken.
radicals.notes: Sits under 日 in 最 and beside 走 in 趣; in 趣 it also supplies the reading シュ.

radicals.meaning: To receive, to accept, to take what is handed over.
radicals.story: A claw-hand 爫 above passing something down across a cover 冖 into the waiting hand 又 below.
radicals.notes: 授 adds a third hand 扌 to make the giving side explicit.

radicals.meaning: mouth; by extension any hole, opening, box, or container
radicals.story: A small open square — the shape your mouth makes saying 'ah', squared off because a brush draws corners faster than curves.
radicals.notes: Not the same as 囗 (enclosure), which is drawn large enough to swallow other elements. When 口 has a line through it, it is 日 or 曰.

radicals.meaning: old, ancient, long-past
radicals.story: Ten (十) mouths (口) — a story told and retold through ten generations of tellers.
radicals.notes: 吉 is 士 over 口, 古 is 十 over 口 — check the top stroke. Distinct from 耂, the stooped 'old man' radical of 老 and 考.

radicals.meaning: call in, summon, invite
radicals.story: A blade (刀) held over a mouth (口) — a sharp order barked out to call someone in.

radicals.meaning: Permission; it may be done.
radicals.story: A mouth 口 with a hooked bar swung out over it — a mouth giving the go-ahead.

radicals.meaning: a raised stand or platform to speak or stand on
radicals.story: A mouth (口) raised on a small base (厶) — the block you stand on to be heard.
radicals.notes: In 始 'begin' and 治 'govern, cure' it is mostly the sound; the modern kanji's 'platform, counter' sense absorbed the older 臺.

radicals.meaning: The court recorder who keeps the annals.
radicals.story: A hand 又 gripping an upright tally straight through the middle — the official who holds the records.
radicals.notes: Deliberately split from 吏 'clerk' and 事 'flagpole', which all descend from the same hand-holding-a-standard picture.

radicals.meaning: The right-hand side.
radicals.story: A hand 𠂇 drawn over a mouth 口 — the hand you eat with.

radicals.meaning: The official who administers and gives the orders.
radicals.story: A mouth 口 tucked under a sheltering hook — the one who issues orders from behind the desk.
radicals.notes: Kept distinct from 史 'scribe' and 吏 'clerk' so the three officials never blur together.

radicals.meaning: each, every, respective; (originally) to arrive
radicals.story: A foot coming down (夂) onto a doorway (口) — arrivals landing on the threshold one after another, each in turn.
radicals.notes: The original sense was 'arrive', which is why it shows up in 客 (a guest arriving under your roof) and 路 (road). 各 vs 名: 各 has 夂 (a foot coming down) on top, 名 has 夕 (evening).

radicals.meaning: Two mouths going at once; clamor.
radicals.story: Two mouths 口 set side by side, both talking straight over each other.

radicals.meaning: fit together, join, match, total
radicals.story: A converging lid (亼) dropped neatly onto a pot's mouth (口) — the click of two things that match.
radicals.notes: Sits at the bottom in 答 and on the right in 給. Its phonetic series is wide: 答 トウ, 給 キュウ, 拾 シュウ, 塔 トウ.

radicals.meaning: An auspicious omen; good fortune.
radicals.story: A samurai (士) standing over a mouth (口) — the word of a warrior is a lucky omen; think of the fortune slips at a shrine.
radicals.notes: Used only in 結 — thread plus good luck is exactly the omikuji knotted onto the shrine rack.

radicals.meaning: same, identical, together, agree
radicals.story: A cover 冂 over 一 and a mouth 口 — read it as everyone under one roof speaking with one voice, hence the same.
radicals.notes: One of the 811. The one-roof-one-voice reading is a memory device, not a claimed etymology — the true origin is unsettled.

radicals.meaning: A petty official; a functionary.
radicals.story: A hand 又 holding up a writing tablet — the low-ranking clerk with his paperwork, drawn almost identically to the scribe 史.

radicals.meaning: Literally 五 over 口; as a character, the archaic 'I, my'.
radicals.story: 五 (five) sitting on 口 (mouth) — five mouths, no more than that; the graph was borrowed to write the old word for 'I'.
radicals.notes: Kept literal so it cannot collide with 我 'ego'. Used only in 語 — five mouths plus words is language.

radicals.meaning: The old Chinese state of Wu (呉), source of the 呉音 readings.
radicals.story: A mouth (口) above a figure with its head thrown back — a loud boast, a graph that came to name the state of Wu.
radicals.variant_notes: Shinjitai of 吳.
radicals.notes: Used only in 誤 (words from Wu, heard wrong — a mistake).

radicals.meaning: circuit, all the way around, lap
radicals.story: A bordered plot packed edge to edge with crops (用) and a mouth (口) beneath it — coverage that reaches every side.
radicals.notes: 同 has the same 冂 frame with 一 above the mouth; 周 fills the frame with a grid.

radicals.meaning: something cracked open into two halves
radicals.story: A sprout pushing up out of a husk (口) that has cracked open beneath it — every character in this family turns on splitting in two.
radicals.notes: 倍 'double' is a person splitting into two; 部 'section, department' is a split-off piece of the village (阝); 剖 'dissect' is the split made with a knife. Watch the bottom: 音 is 立 over 日, 咅 is 立 over 口.

radicals.meaning: all together, every one (originally: to shout as one)
radicals.story: A broad-bladed dagger-axe (戌) raised over an open mouth (口) — troops roaring in a single voice, which is where the old sense 'all together' comes from.
radicals.notes: Not 成 'become': 咸 has a 口 tucked inside the weapon, 成 does not. Sits on the right in 減 but on top in 感.

radicals.meaning: One person counted onto a roster; staff, personnel.
radicals.story: A mouth (口) sitting on a cowrie shell (貝) — one more head counted onto the payroll.
radicals.notes: Used only in 損 (a hand taking a member away — loss).

radicals.meaning: To call out repeatedly; the original graph behind 歌.
radicals.story: 可 stacked on top of 可 — the same call given twice over, a repeated chant.
radicals.notes: Keyed to 'chant' rather than 'song' so it stays distinct from the kanji 歌. Used only in 歌.

radicals.meaning: The base of a plant stalk.
radicals.story: A pointed cap over 冂 enclosing 古 — the old graph for the base of a plant stalk, surviving in Japanese only as a テキ sound-marker.
radicals.notes: Distinct from 商 (which has 口 not 古 at the bottom). Used only in 適.

radicals.meaning: tall and curving, lofty
radicals.story: A bending figure 夭 crowning a tall-building shape — height with a curve at the top, an arch.
radicals.notes: 'High arch' is chosen over the adjective 'lofty' because wood 木 + high arch composes 橋 'bridge' on its own.

radicals.meaning: an enclosing wall; a fully sealed square
radicals.story: A square closed on all four sides — the rampart built the whole way round a walled town, shutting in whatever stands inside.
radicals.notes: Written larger than 口 (mouth) and always wraps something. A real wall in 国, 困, 囲, 図; a borrowed shape in 四 and 因.

radicals.meaning: No independent meaning; the boxed lower body of 面.
radicals.story: A rectangular frame with a stroke down the middle and lines ruled across it — the outline of a face with its features drawn inside.
radicals.variant_notes: CJKVI matches this shape to a variant of 回; inside 面 it is simply the outline of the face, so treat it as shape.

radicals.meaning: Hard, firm, solid, fixed in place.
radicals.story: Something old 古 walled in on all four sides 囗 — nothing gets in or out, so it holds firm.

radicals.meaning: earth, soil, ground; land, dirt
radicals.story: A long bottom stroke for the surface of the ground with a shorter one heaped above it, skewered by a vertical — a clod of earth sitting on the field.
radicals.notes: The classic trap: 土 (soil) has a SHORT top stroke and a long bottom; 士 (samurai) is the reverse — long on top, short below.

radicals.meaning: warp threads stretched on a loom (Japanese squashed form of 巠)
radicals.story: As written in Japanese it is a hand (又) pressed onto soil (土), but it is a flattened 巠, which drew the warp threads pulled taut down a loom frame.
radicals.variant_notes: 巠 is the full original form — three warp threads under a bar, mounted on a stand (工). Japanese shinjitai always squashes it to 圣 (又 over 土) in 経, 軽, 径, 茎.
radicals.notes: 圣 is also the Chinese simplified form of 聖 'holy' — unrelated to its Japanese use here.

radicals.meaning: The tapering jade baton a noble held at court.
radicals.story: Two mounds of earth (土) stacked one on the other — the pointed jade baton raised at court, cut from the ground up.
radicals.notes: Keyed to 'scepter' rather than 'jade' so it cannot collide with 玉. Used only in 街, inside the crossroads 行.

radicals.meaning: To sit down on the ground.
radicals.story: Two people 人 planted side by side on the soil 土 — squatting down together.
radicals.notes: Sits in the crook of 广 in 座, supplying both the sound ザ and the sitting.

radicals.meaning: To hang down, to dangle.
radicals.story: A plant with all its stems and leaves sagging down toward the soil 土 beneath.
radicals.notes: 垂 also carries the sense of the far frontier — the drooping edge of the realm — which suits the post-stations of 郵.

radicals.meaning: to set a seedling into the ground (ancestor of 芸/藝)
radicals.story: A kneeling figure with grasping hands 丸 pressing a sapling into a mound of earth 坴 — the original picture of planting.
radicals.notes: Easily confused with 執; 埶 has 坴 (earth mound) on the left, 執 has 幸.

radicals.meaning: samurai, gentleman, scholar-official; -ist, professional
radicals.story: A broad blade resting on a narrower base — an axe head stood upright, the emblem of the gentleman-warrior.
radicals.notes: 士 vs 土: in 士 (samurai) the TOP stroke is the long one; in 土 (soil) the BOTTOM stroke is. The samurai wears the broad shoulders up top.

radicals.meaning: A shaft that bulges in the middle where the load rides.
radicals.story: A straight post whose middle stroke swells outward, like a shoulder pole bowing under its burden; in 任 a person 亻 steps up and shoulders it.
radicals.notes: The ninth calendar stem; also read by some as a weaving bobbin, which is the same swollen-shaft picture.

radicals.meaning: sell, put up for sale
radicals.story: The full form 賣 was 出 'put out' over 貝 'shell-money' — goods put out for cash — which the shinjitai squashes into a topknot (士) over a canopy (冖) over a pair of legs (儿), a vendor standing behind a covered stall.
radicals.variant_notes: 賣 is the traditional full form (出 over 貝), still seen in older printing; 売 is the shinjitai used everywhere in modern Japanese, including inside 続 and 読.
radicals.notes: In 続 and 読 it carries only sound (ゾク, ドク) — nothing is being sold there.

radicals.meaning: A drum standing on its stand.
radicals.story: A drum mounted on a pedestal with ornaments fluttering at the top — the same drum that sits inside 鼓.
radicals.notes: 喜 is drums above and a singing mouth 口 below — noise-making is joy. Distinguish from 豆, which is the bare pedestal bowl without the drum's top ornaments.

radicals.meaning: a foot coming down from above; arriving, following, being late
radicals.story: A foot pointing downward — the short stroke is the ankle and the long sweep is the sole dragging behind, someone stepping down into the character from above.
radicals.variant_notes: 夂 (Kangxi 34) and 夊 (Kangxi 35) are separate radicals in theory but are written the same way and merged in practice; treat them as one primitive.
radicals.notes: Look for lateness or arrival: 冬, 各, 後, 夏, 変, 愛. Against 攵 (whip): 夂 has three strokes and sits at the top, 攵 has four and sits on the right.

radicals.meaning: Coming down, descending.
radicals.story: Two footprints stacked one under the other, both toes pointing down the slope.
radicals.notes: Beside the mound 阝 in 降 the feet are literally walking down the hill.

radicals.meaning: to return, to repeat, to go over again
radicals.story: A squat bellows — the lidded box in the middle — with a foot (夂) trailing below to work it; the exact origin is disputed, so hold onto the image of something pumped again and again.
radicals.notes: A very reliable sound element: 腹, 複, 復, 覆 all read フク.

radicals.meaning: evening, dusk, nightfall
radicals.story: The crescent 月 with one inner stroke rubbed out — a thin moon just showing at dusk.
radicals.notes: 夕 vs 月: the evening moon is open at the bottom and has only one inner stroke. 名 is a mouth calling in the dark because you cannot see who it is; 多 is two evenings piled up.

radicals.meaning: Many, much, numerous.
radicals.story: Two evenings 夕 stacked one on the other — nights piling up until there are a great many.
radicals.notes: 移 takes 多 as its sound element even though the modern readings (タ vs イ) have drifted apart.

radicals.meaning: Night, evening.
radicals.story: A person tucked under a lid 亠 with the evening moon 夕 hanging at their side — bedded down for the night.
radicals.notes: Keep 'night' apart from 夕 'evening' — 夕 is the single moon-sliver, 夜 is the whole night.

radicals.meaning: big, large, great
radicals.story: A person 人 planted with both arms flung out wide — as big as a body can make itself.
radicals.notes: The whole family hangs on one added mark: 太 (fat) has a dot between the legs, 犬 (dog) has a dot on the shoulder, 天 (heaven) has a line over the head.

radicals.meaning: husband; grown man
radicals.story: A grown person (大) with a hairpin (一) driven through the topknot — the coming-of-age pin that marks an adult man.
radicals.notes: 夫 vs 天: 夫's top bar CROSSES the vertical (the pin goes through the hair); 天's sits on top of it. 夫 vs 失: 失's top stroke slants away as a slash.

radicals.meaning: the notched thumb-ring that hooks a bowstring; to release, to decide
radicals.story: A hand wearing the notched jade thumb-ring an archer uses to hook the bowstring, caught at the instant the string is released.
radicals.notes: 決 'decide' is water bursting through the breach once the ring lets go; 快 'pleasant' is the heart's string released.

radicals.meaning: A bending, swaying figure; young and supple.
radicals.story: A person 大 with the head tilted and the arms swung over to one side — a figure bending or dancing.
radicals.notes: 笑 is bamboo swaying above a body bent double — the standard reading of this element in 笑 is the bending posture of laughter.

radicals.meaning: center, middle, midpoint
radicals.story: A person (大) with a yoke laid straight across the shoulders, pinned at the dead middle of the load.
radicals.notes: Note the reading split: 央 itself is オウ, but as a sound component it hands out エイ (英, 映).

radicals.meaning: To let slip, lose, miss.
radicals.story: A hand with one stroke sliding out past its grip — something dropped and gone.
radicals.notes: Used only in 鉄. Be aware that there 失 is a shinjitai stand-in (鐵 → 鉄) and carries neither the meaning nor the sound — the mnemonic 'the metal you lose to rust' is a memory hook, not an etymology.

radicals.meaning: woman, female; daughter, wife
radicals.story: A kneeling figure with arms crossed in front and a skirt sweeping out — a woman seated, drawn in three strokes.
radicals.notes: Usually the left radical (妹, 姉, 始, 婚) but also sits at the bottom (安, 妻, 要, 委).

radicals.meaning: a captive put to forced labour; slave, servant
radicals.story: A woman (女) seized from behind by a hand (又) — a captive taken and put to work.
radicals.notes: Sits on top in 努 'exertion' (slave + power) and 怒 'anger' (slave + heart), carrying both the image and the ド sound.

radicals.meaning: At ease, calm, unhurried.
radicals.story: The sun 日 resting directly over a woman 女 — a lady taking her ease in the daylight.
radicals.notes: In 宴 it gives the sound エン, and its 'at ease' sense suits a feast under the roof 宀.

radicals.meaning: A maidservant or concubine.
radicals.story: A woman 女 with a standing figure 立 planted directly over her — the maid who waits on someone else.
radicals.notes: The top is traditionally explained as a clipped 辛 (a branding needle), but the shape as written is simply 立 over 女.

radicals.meaning: No independent sense in Japanese — rice heaped on a woman.
radicals.story: Rice (米) heaped on top of a woman (女) — a lapful of grain, and nothing more; this is just the squashed form of 婁.
radicals.variant_notes: Shinjitai squash of 婁.
radicals.notes: Used only in 数 — a woman counting grains of rice while a taskmaster (攵) stands over her.

radicals.meaning: child, infant; offspring
radicals.story: A swaddled infant — a big round head on top, arms flung out sideways as the crossbar, and the wrapped legs drawn as one curling stroke.
radicals.notes: 子 vs 了: 了 is the same hooked body WITHOUT the outstretched arms.

radicals.meaning: A child's devotion to a parent.
radicals.story: An old man 耂 leaning his weight on the child 子 who props him up from below.
radicals.notes: 教 adds the strike-hand 攵: filial duty beaten into the pupil.

radicals.meaning: The eldest child, first in the line.
radicals.story: A child 子 sitting over a basin 皿 — the shape used to write 'eldest child'.
radicals.notes: Sound element in 猛 (モウ), which puts a wild beast 犭 in front of it.

radicals.meaning: a roofed building; house, home, indoors, shelter
radicals.story: A dot for the ridge-pole with two eaves sweeping down either side — a roof seen head-on, always sitting over whatever it shelters.
radicals.notes: Called うかんむり. 冖 (crown) is the same lid without the dot on top; 广 (lean-to) drops its left side into a bare downstroke.

radicals.meaning: A rack or chest for putting things away.
radicals.story: A roof (宀) over a nail-hook (丁) — the old picture of a storing rack, a chest where things get stowed.
radicals.notes: Used only in 貯 (shells stowed in the chest — savings).

radicals.meaning: Complete, whole, finished.
radicals.story: A roof 宀 raised over 元 — the building is topped out and the job is done.

radicals.meaning: Still, silent, secluded.
radicals.story: A pierced heart 必 shut in under a roof 宀 — a room so quiet you can hear the heartbeat.
radicals.notes: 密 adds a mountain 山 behind the hushed room: hidden away and dense.

radicals.meaning: government official; public office
radicals.story: Under a roof (宀) sits a heaped mound of stores (𠂤) — the walled office building where the state kept its officials and their supplies.
radicals.notes: The same mound 𠂤 turns up in 追 and 師. Not 宮 'palace', which has two 口 stacked under the roof.

radicals.meaning: guest, visitor, customer, passenger
radicals.story: Under a roof 宀, a foot comes down to a mouth 口 (各, 'arrive') — someone who has turned up at your house.
radicals.notes: One of the 811. In 額 it is the カク→ガク sound only.

radicals.meaning: Harm, damage, injury.
radicals.story: Something cutting down through a roof 宀 and into the mouth 口 beneath it — the household comes to grief.
radicals.notes: 割 adds the knife 刂 and takes the カツ reading from this element.

radicals.meaning: The third earthly branch, the Tiger (とら).
radicals.story: Under a roof (宀), two hands hold an arrow (矢) upright — the graph used for 寅, the Tiger of the twelve branches.
radicals.notes: Parallel to 戌 'zodiac dog'. Used only in 演.

radicals.meaning: thumb; the hand doing careful, measured work (the old 'inch' measure)
radicals.story: A hand (又, flattened out) with a tick marking the pulse point one thumb's width below the palm — read it as the thumb itself, the hand doing precise work.
radicals.notes: Traditionally glossed 'inch'. Always picture the thumb instead — it keeps 付 (hand giving), 対 (hands facing) and 導 (a guiding hand) concrete.

radicals.meaning: Buddhist temple
radicals.story: Ground (土) worked over by a steady hand (寸) — the carefully tended plot that became a temple compound.
radicals.notes: As a component it never means 'temple' — it is pure sound: 持 ジ, 時 ジ, 詩 シ, 待 タイ, 等 トウ, 特 トク. 待 (wait, with 彳 going) vs 持 (hold, with 扌 hand) is a classic mix-up: check the left side.

radicals.meaning: To pick something up between the fingers.
radicals.story: A downturned claw 爫 closing onto a thumb 寸 — fingers pinching something up.
radicals.notes: The right side of 将 is worn down in the modern shape; the pinching hand is the memory hook, not a claim about what 将 means.

radicals.meaning: A military commander; also 'about to, shall'.
radicals.story: A plank bed (丬) with a slab of meat (夕) and a hand (寸) beside it — the commander carving up the ration and handing it out.
radicals.variant_notes: Shinjitai of 將.
radicals.notes: Used only in 奨 (a big reward from the general — encouragement).

radicals.meaning: A hand pressing a hot iron on cloth; as a character, a military officer rank.
radicals.story: A hand (寸) pressing a heated block (示) down beneath a flat slab (尸) — smoothing cloth with a hot iron.
radicals.notes: As a standalone character 尉 is the officer rank in 中尉 (lieutenant), but the ironing image is its graphic origin and is exactly what makes 慰 work: pressing the wrinkles out of a heart is consolation. Used only in 慰.

radicals.meaning: small, little, minor
radicals.story: A short vertical spine with a tiny flake chipped off each side — something whittled down to almost nothing.
radicals.variant_notes: 小 stands alone or sits at the bottom; ⺌ is the flattened top form used in 当 and 尚. The three-dot 𭕄 on top of 学, 労 and 覚 looks similar but comes from a different element.
radicals.notes: The 小 at the foot of 京, 県, 原 and 歳 is a worn-down remnant of other shapes, not the meaning 'small'.

radicals.meaning: few, a little, scant
radicals.story: 小 'small' with one more stroke shaving off the corner — small, then cut down even further.
radicals.notes: 省 'inspect, omit' is few + eye — looking with only a squint; 歩 'walk' is a footprint (止) over the same shape.

radicals.meaning: A sacrificial signal fire.
radicals.story: A crossed frame of stacked logs with sparks (小) flying out below — a signal fire blazing.
radicals.notes: The original graph behind 燎. Used only in 寮 (a lodging with a fire under its roof — dormitory).

radicals.meaning: A mark that makes something stand out; a fault, blame.
radicals.story: A bent arm-shape with a single dot stuck onto it — the one mark that catches the eye.
radicals.notes: 尤 means both 'outstanding' and 'fault'; in 就 it supplies neither a clean sound nor a clear meaning, so lean on the marked shape.

radicals.meaning: a slumped body; but in most characters, the roof and wall of a dwelling
radicals.story: A figure seen from the side, bent at the hips with its legs folded away underneath — a body lying down, which is why the radical is named 'corpse'.
radicals.notes: Called しかばね. In 屋, 局, 居, 届, 展 it acts as a building, not a body — several of those descend from 戶 'door'. 戸 is this shape with a lid stroke added on top.

radicals.meaning: A hand gripping the staff of office.
radicals.story: Fingers ヨ closed around a long diagonal shaft — the staff carried by whoever is in charge.

radicals.meaning: the shaku foot-measure; a measuring length
radicals.story: A hand at the top with the thumb stretched out and down, spanning the old foot-measure it names — picture a folding yardstick.
radicals.notes: Important: in 択, 沢, 訳, 釈 and 駅 this 尺 is a post-war simplification of 睪, which is why those readings (タク, ヤク, シャク, エキ) scatter. In 昼 it is a leftover from 晝.

radicals.meaning: A roofed building; a shop or the trade carried on in it.
radicals.story: A slanting awning (尸) pulled down over 至 (arrive) — the roofed place you arrive at, the shop on the corner.
radicals.notes: Keyed to 'shop' rather than 'roof' so that 'roof' stays reserved for 宀. Used only in 握 (a hand grabbing at the shop).

radicals.meaning: Rain getting in under the roof.
radicals.story: Rain (雨) falling underneath a roof slab (尸) — water coming in where it should not.
radicals.notes: Used only in 漏 — this is genuinely the original graph of 'leak', with 氵 added later.

radicals.meaning: a young shoot breaking through the ground
radicals.story: A single shoot pushing up out of the soil, its first two leaves opening on either side of the stem.
radicals.notes: In 出 the shape is not really a sprout — 出 drew a foot stepping out of a hollow (凵) — but 屮 is the standard name for these three strokes.

radicals.meaning: mountain, hill
radicals.story: Three peaks rising from a single baseline with the middle one tallest — a mountain range in silhouette.
radicals.notes: Sits on top in 炭, 島 and 密; note 出 is two 山 stacked, not one.

radicals.meaning: river, stream
radicals.story: Two banks with a current running down between them — three strokes of flowing water.
radicals.variant_notes: 巛 is the curled three-stroke form used on top (as in 災); 川 is the standalone and left-hand form.

radicals.meaning: An islet standing up in midstream; hence a province.
radicals.story: The river 川 with a dot dropped into each channel — sandbars breaking the surface of the current.

radicals.meaning: craft, construction,工作; a builder's tool and the work done with it
radicals.story: Two horizontal bars joined by a single vertical — a carpenter's square stood on end, or the I-beam it will help put up.
radicals.notes: A strong sound component: 江, 紅, 攻, 功 are all コウ and 空 is クウ. 土 (soil) has a longer bottom stroke and a shorter top; 工's two bars are close to equal.

radicals.meaning: hold firmly, bind tight
radicals.story: A craftsman's tool 工 held inside 凡 — the flattened picture of a hand gripping the work tight, a clamp.
radicals.notes: Serves as the phonetic in 筑/築. 'Clamp' avoids any collision with the hand primitives 又, 扌, 手, 爫.

radicals.meaning: self, oneself; a knotted record cord
radicals.story: A cord bent back on itself twice — the knotted string a person kept as their own private record.
radicals.notes: 己/已/巳 differ only in how far the top-left stroke closes: 己 fully open, 已 half closed, 巳 fully closed. As a component it is sound, not meaning: 記 キ; the shapes in 改 and 配 come from 巳/卩 instead.

radicals.meaning: The snake, sixth of the twelve earthly branches.
radicals.story: The same coiled shape as 己 but sealed shut at the top — a snake curled up tight.
radicals.notes: Modern 起 is written with 己; CJKVI records the older 巳. Keep 'serpent' clearly apart from whatever keyword 己 carries.

radicals.meaning: a huge snake (traditional gloss); a coiled, swollen shape
radicals.story: Traditionally glossed as a giant snake — see a coiled body (the 己-like tail) with a swollen belly from the meal it just swallowed.
radicals.notes: In 色 the shape reads as a kneeling figure rather than a snake; in 把 it is pure sound ハ.

radicals.meaning: A narrow lane between houses; the back streets.
radicals.story: 共 (a load hoisted by many hands) over a bent 巳 — a crooked lane where the whole neighbourhood squeezes past one another.
radicals.notes: Used only in 港 (the water-alleys of a harbour).

radicals.meaning: two figures set out side by side; the wind trigram, compliance
radicals.story: Two small kneeling figures placed side by side on a pair of raised hands 共 — a matched pair presented for inspection.
radicals.notes: The 'pair presented for inspection' image feeds 選 'choose' directly.

radicals.meaning: cloth, fabric; a hanging piece of woven material
radicals.story: A rectangle of cloth hung off a rail, the long vertical being the fold running down its middle — a towel on a hook.
radicals.notes: Cloth is the thread: 布 (linen), 帯 (sash), 帳 (curtain/ledger), 席 (mat), 幣 (banknote). 中 has its vertical run right through an enclosed box; 巾's vertical hangs from an open frame.

radicals.meaning: A band that goes all the way around; one full circuit.
radicals.story: A cloth 巾 with a bar laid clean across the top — a band wrapped right the way round.
radicals.variant_notes: 帀 is the old form of 匝 'to encircle'.

radicals.meaning: A market; a city.
radicals.story: A lid 亠 pulled over a hanging cloth 巾 — the awning and curtains of a market stall.
radicals.variant_notes: In 姉 the right side is historically 巿 (a knee-apron, written with one stroke running through), but modern Japanese printing shows 市.

radicals.meaning: Cloth; a bolt of woven fabric.
radicals.story: A hand 𠂇 laid across a hanging towel 巾 — cloth being smoothed out flat.
radicals.notes: Uses the Heisig keyword 'linen' so it never collides with 巾.

radicals.meaning: broom, sweeping
radicals.story: A hand (彐) gripping the handle above a cloth (巾), with the straw bundle tied on in the middle.

radicals.meaning: sovereign, supreme ruler, high god
radicals.story: A crown 亠 and 丷 stacked over 冖 and a cloth 巾 — the origin is disputed (probably an altar-stand for the high god), so picture an emperor in full regalia.
radicals.notes: Distinct from 王 'king'. In 締 it is the テイ sound.

radicals.meaning: shield, forked stave; (later sense) to dry
radicals.story: A forked pole with two crossbars — the hand-held stave a soldier thrust out to block a blow; the modern 'dry' sense (干す) is a later use of the same shape.
radicals.notes: Not 千 'thousand': 千 opens with a slanting 丿, 干 with a flat 一. A dependable カン: 刊, 汗, 肝, 幹.

radicals.meaning: One year.
radicals.story: Read the strokes as a stalk of grain 禾 bent over a person hauling it home — one harvest carried in is one year.

radicals.meaning: happiness, good fortune; graphically a pair of manacles
radicals.story: The old graph is usually read as a pair of manacles, the cuff and its locking bar — and the good fortune is in not being the one wearing them.
radicals.notes: The keyword is 'handcuffs' because that is what 執 'take hold' and 報 'requital, report' are built on; the kanji's own meaning is 'happiness'. Against 辛 'bitter': 幸 has 土 on top, 辛 has 立.

radicals.meaning: a tiny twist of silk; small, young
radicals.story: A little loop of silk twisted at the top with its tail hanging below — the upper half of the full thread 糸.
radicals.notes: A skein is a small coil of yarn: 糸 is the full thread, 幺 the miniature.

radicals.meaning: how many, how much; the slightest amount, the subtle
radicals.story: Two tiny thread-coils 幺幺 beside a guard with a halberd 戍 — a sentry counting the faintest signs, hence 'how many'.
radicals.notes: The keyword is abstract but is the long-established one (Heisig, Tofugu, WaniKani all use 'how many'); when writing the 機 mnemonic, lean on the sentry-and-threads picture from the story rather than the bare phrase.

radicals.meaning: a building open at the front; a hall, shop, or shelter built against a slope
radicals.story: A dot on a roof whose left side drops away into a single bare downstroke — a shed leaning against a hillside, walled at the back and wide open at the front.
radicals.notes: Called まだれ. 厂 (cliff) is the same shape with no dot; 疒 (sickness) adds two small strokes inside. Everything under 广 is a building: 広, 店, 府, 席, 座, 庭.

radicals.meaning: A hand ticking off a length; hence degree, extent, an occasion.
radicals.story: Under a lean-to shelter (广), a hand (又) reaches out past a measuring bar — the hand marking off a length.
radicals.notes: As a standalone kanji 度 is 'degree'; the primitive is keyed to the hand-measuring image because 'water + degree' licenses no picture for 渡, whereas 'measuring the depth by hand before crossing' does.

radicals.meaning: the legendary one-horned judgment beast (xiezhi)
radicals.story: A single horn up top over a long body and four legs — the mythical ox-like creature of ancient law courts.
radicals.notes: 薦 is literally the grass this beast was fed, which is how it came to mean 'offer, recommend' — so the mnemonic writes itself.

radicals.meaning: to stride, to extend, a long pace
radicals.story: A leg pulled out into an exaggerated step: 辶 (road) with its dots stripped off and its base stroke stretched long.
radicals.notes: Heisig's keyword is 'stretch'. Wraps the bottom-left of the character (建・延). Keep it apart from 辶 (road) and 彳.

radicals.meaning: The palace courtyard; a court of law.
radicals.story: A figure standing 𡈼 at the end of a long stretching stride 廴 — the open yard where the ruler receives people.

radicals.meaning: two hands raised from below, holding something up
radicals.story: A pair of hands side by side, palms up, lifting whatever sits above them.
radicals.notes: 廾 has two uprights rising past one bar; 廿 (twenty) has them hanging below the bar.

radicals.meaning: twenty — two tens fused into one block
radicals.story: Two 十 'ten' fused shoulder to shoulder into one block — twenty written in a single unit.
radicals.notes: As a character it genuinely means twenty, but inside 度 'degree' and 席 'seat' it is only the crushed top of an older element — a shape. Do not mix it with 廾 (a pair of cupped hands) or 艹 (grass).

radicals.meaning: two uprights under crossbars; (historically) level, even
