radicals.story: Two uprights standing under a pair of crossbars — the silhouette of a torii gate; historically this was 幵, two pegs filed to exactly the same level.
radicals.variant_notes: 幵 is the older full form (two 干 side by side); 开 is the modern compressed shape used in Japanese printing.
radicals.notes: Reliable ケン/ケイ sound in 研 and 形. In 開 (open) it is really 廾, two hands lifting the bar out of the gate — a different source that happens to land on the same shape.

radicals.meaning: a tethering stake or post
radicals.story: A short post with a brace slanting off it and a tick at the top — a stake driven into the ground to tie something to.
radicals.notes: It was the historical sound element in 代 and 式, but the Japanese readings (ダイ, シキ) no longer match, so lean on the stake image.

radicals.meaning: A fixed form — ceremony, formula, style.
radicals.story: A carpenter's square (工) with a stake (弋) planted beside it — work done to one fixed pattern, the formal ritual.
radicals.notes: Used only in 試 (words put to a set form — a test).

radicals.meaning: an archer's bow
radicals.story: A bowstave curved back on itself in three strokes, waiting for its string.
radicals.notes: Archery, not bowing. 引 is the bow plus the drawn string, so it means 'pull'.

radicals.meaning: Graphically two poles lashed by a cord; in Japanese, the ateji for ドル (dollar).
radicals.story: Two crooked poles lashed together by a cord running through them — the shape looks so much like $ that Japanese borrowed 弗 to write 'dollar'.
radicals.notes: 弗 is a real, standard Japanese ateji for ドル — this is not an invented resemblance. Used only in 費 (dollars over shells — expense).

radicals.meaning: (shape) a pig's snout in profile, or a squashed hand
radicals.story: Three strokes forming an open bracket — Kangxi names it a pig's snout seen from the side, though in most modern kanji it is really a hand with the fingers drawn as bars.
radicals.variant_notes: 彑 is the pointed-top variant (彙); ⺕ is the same three-stroke bracket as it appears inside 雪, 争, 帰 and 録.
radicals.notes: In 当 it is neither snout nor hand but a leftover from simplifying 當 — a shape only, which is why no single meaning fits it.

radicals.meaning: to draw up and strain water; carve, set down
radicals.story: A hand 彐 above falling drops 氺 — the original object is disputed, so read it as a bucket hauled up from a well and still dripping.
radicals.notes: Honest shape reading — the well-bucket account is one of several, and the story says so.

radicals.meaning: hair, fine lines, streaks, ornament
radicals.story: Three parallel strokes all curving the same way — a lock of flowing hair, and by extension any engraved line, streak or decorative pattern.
radicals.notes: Always on the right. In 形 and 彫 the 'hair' is really the ornamental scoring on a shape; in 修 it is grooming.

radicals.meaning: a fine-looking man of talent and accomplishment
radicals.story: A patterned brow 文 under a cliff-like forehead 厂, with three combed strokes 彡 for the hair — the old word for a good-looking gentleman.
radicals.notes: Carries both the sound and the 'face' sense into 顔; watch the top against 産, which takes 生 underneath instead of 彡.

radicals.meaning: going, walking, travelling along a road
radicals.story: The left half of the crossroads 行, chopped straight down the middle — one side of a street, which is why every character with it is about going somewhere.
radicals.notes: Called ぎょうにんべん. Three strokes, versus two for 亻 (standing person) — the extra flick at the top is the tell.

radicals.meaning: heart; mind, feeling, emotion, intention
radicals.story: A curved bowl with three sparks flying off it — the heart muscle drawn with its chambers and the vessels shooting out.
radicals.variant_notes: 心 stands alone or sits at the bottom (思, 念, 急); 忄 (りっしんべん) is the upright left-side form (性, 情, 快); ⺗ is the rare squashed bottom form (恭, 慕).
radicals.notes: In Japanese the heart is the seat of thought as well as feeling — read it as 'mind' wherever 'heart' sounds sentimental. 必 is this heart with a slash driven through it.

radicals.meaning: heart, feelings; the left-hand form of 心
radicals.story: The heart 心 stood on end and squeezed thin so it can run down the left edge — a heart hammering against the ribs.
radicals.variant_notes: 心 is the full form, used alone or at the bottom (思, 急); 忄 is the three-stroke form on the left (忙, 快, 情); ⺗ is the flattened bottom form of a few characters such as 恭.
radicals.notes: 忄 vs 扌: the heart's two side ticks sit high and slant apart; the hand 扌 has one bar straight across with a hook at the foot. Every 忄 kanji is about an emotion.

radicals.meaning: Certainly, without fail.
radicals.story: A heart 心 with one stroke driven straight through it — a resolve nailed so firmly it has to happen.
radicals.notes: The graphic origin of 必 is disputed; the pierced heart is a memory hook, not scholarship.

radicals.meaning: To bear it, put up with, hold back.
radicals.story: A blade (刃) resting flat on a heart (心) — bearing it without flinching.
radicals.notes: The same 忍 as in 忍者 (ninja). Used only in 認 (enduring what is said until you finally acknowledge it).

radicals.meaning: To be unworthy of the honour you were given.
radicals.story: A heart 㣺 flattened out beneath heaven 天 — bowing so low you feel undeserving.
radicals.notes: Pure sound element in 添 (テン).

radicals.meaning: sorrow, anxiety, mourning
radicals.story: A drooping head 頁 under a cover, a heart 心, and dragging feet 夂 — a person trudging along under the weight of grief.
radicals.notes: 優 is a person 亻 acting out grief — the mourner-performer, which is exactly where its 'actor' and 'gentle, excellent' senses come from.

radicals.meaning: dagger-axe, halberd; weapon, war
radicals.story: A long pole with an axe blade lashed crosswise near the top and a tassel flicking off the upper corner — the Chinese ge, a blade mounted sideways on a stick.
radicals.notes: A real weapon: think 'war axe on a stick', swung not thrust — that is what separates it from 矛 (halberd). Heads the 成・我・戦 family; 弋 is the same shape minus the top stroke.

radicals.meaning: A broad-bladed war axe.
radicals.story: A halberd (戈) with its blade swelled out into a broad crescent — the big-bladed war axe, ancestor of 鉞.
radicals.notes: Deliberately distinguished from 戈 (halberd) and 戌 (zodiac dog). Used only in 越.

radicals.meaning: A wide-bladed war axe (the fifth calendar stem).
radicals.story: The halberd 戈 drawn with its blade swollen into a broad sweeping edge — a heavy chopping axe rather than a spear.

radicals.meaning: The eleventh earthly branch, the Dog (いぬ); graphically a broad axe.
radicals.story: A halberd (戈) with an extra stroke closing off its top — the shape is an old broad axe, but it is known above all as 戌, the Dog of the twelve branches.
radicals.notes: Named for the branch rather than the axe so it stays distinct from 戉 'battle axe'. Used only in 歳, wrapped around 小.

radicals.meaning: To become, to be completed, to achieve.
radicals.story: A halberd 戊 with a pin 丁 driven through it — the weapon fitted together and finished.
radicals.notes: 盛 puts it over a dish 皿 — heaped until the dish becomes full.

radicals.meaning: I, me, oneself.
radicals.story: A hand (𠂉) gripping a saw-toothed halberd (戈) — a weapon graph borrowed to write 'I, me'.
radicals.notes: Used only in 義 — a sheep (𦍌) offered up over my own self, hence righteousness.

radicals.meaning: To guard, to warn; a precept.
radicals.story: A halberd 戈 gripped in two hands 廾 — a guard standing watch.
radicals.notes: Distinguish from 兵: 兵 is an axe 斤 in two hands, 戒 is a halberd 戈 in two hands.

radicals.meaning: a marked-off territory held under arms; later borrowed for 'a certain one'
radicals.story: A halberd (戈) standing guard over a marked-off patch of ground (口 with its boundary line) — one guard, one territory; this is the original of 国 'country'.
radicals.notes: 域 'region' re-adds the soil (土) once 或 drifted to mean 'a certain'; 惑 'bewilderment' is a heart still patrolling its borders, unable to settle.

radicals.meaning: (no independent use in modern Japanese) the emblem element of 職, 識, 織
radicals.story: A halberd (戈) with a marked pennant (音) lashed to its shaft — the standard by which a unit is recognised, which is why it turns up in 職 'post', 識 'recognise' and 織 'weave'.
radicals.notes: Counted as 12 strokes to match this app's totals (職 18画, 識 19画). It never stands alone in Japanese, so learn it only as this banner shape.

radicals.meaning: door, one door-panel; household
radicals.story: A single hinged door-panel with its lintel across the top — half of the double gate 門.
radicals.variant_notes: 戸 is the modern Japanese form; 戶 is the traditional form with a slanting top stroke, seen in older printing and in Chinese.
radicals.notes: 戸 vs 尸: the door has a dot or short stroke on top; 尸 (the flag/corpse shape of 局, 居, 屋) does not.

radicals.meaning: To go back, to come back, to restore.
radicals.story: A door 戸 with 大 crouched underneath it — the older form wrote 犬, a dog squeezing back in beneath the door.
radicals.variant_notes: 戻 is the shinjitai of 戾, which had 犬 where 戻 now has 大.
radicals.notes: 涙 is water that comes back to the eyes.

radicals.meaning: hand; a hand's work, a move
radicals.story: Four fingers drawn as three horizontal strokes crossed by the wrist and forearm — a hand held up palm-out.
radicals.variant_notes: 扌 is the compressed left-hand form used in the great majority of hand verbs (打, 押, 持); 手 keeps its full shape when standing alone or sitting at the bottom (挙, 摩); 龵 is a rare top-position variant.
radicals.notes: 手 vs 毛: 毛 (fur) flips the final stroke so the tail sweeps to the RIGHT and up; 手 hooks to the left.

radicals.meaning: hand; grabbing, holding, doing something manual
radicals.story: A hand 手 crushed into three strokes: the vertical hook is the forearm and the two crossing strokes are the fingers curled around it.
radicals.variant_notes: 手 is the free-standing kanji 'hand'; 扌 (てへん) is its left-side form and appears in almost every verb of manipulation (打, 押, 担, 投).
radicals.notes: Parent is 手. 才 (talent) is nearly identical — 扌 hooks upward at the bottom of the vertical and its top stroke is a short rising flick.

radicals.meaning: talent, natural ability; also the age counter
radicals.story: A seedling breaking the soil line with a stroke crossing it — raw ability already showing before anything has grown.
radicals.notes: 才 vs 扌: the hand 扌 has a plain vertical hook with a bar straight across; 才 adds a rising slash out of the crossing. In 閉 the 才 is really a bar bolted across the gate, not talent.

radicals.meaning: Taking something over from whoever held it before.
radicals.story: Read as a shape: a hook 了 clamped in the middle while finger-strokes close in from both sides, like a baton being passed hand to hand.
radicals.notes: Often explained as hands lifting a kneeling person, but that reading is not certain enough to state as fact.

radicals.meaning: branch, offshoot; to support, prop up
radicals.story: A hand (又) at the bottom gripping a snapped-off twig (十) above it — the branch you have just broken off, held up like a prop.
radicals.notes: One keyword covers both senses: a branch off a trunk, and propping something up. In 技 it is doing sound work (シ→ギ), not meaning.

radicals.meaning: striking, forcing, making something happen to someone
radicals.story: A hand (the two strokes at the lower right) gripping a stick that is raised above it — an arm caught mid-swing.
radicals.variant_notes: 攴 is the full ancient form (a hand 又 under a raised rod); 攵 (のぶん) is the everyday right-side form. Same primitive.
radicals.notes: Nearly always on the right (改, 攻, 放, 政, 教, 救). 文 (writing) has a lid 亠 on top; 夂 (trailing foot) is one stroke shorter and sits on TOP of characters.

radicals.meaning: imperial order, command to set things right
radicals.story: A tied bundle 束 under a striking hand 攵 — an order laid down to whip things into line.
radicals.variant_notes: 勅 is the standard modern Japanese form; the older shape 敕 is what survives inside 整.
radicals.notes: Semantic only — 敕 チョク does not supply 整's セイ.

radicals.meaning: Worn out, ragged, shabby.
radicals.story: A cloth (巾) with fibres flying off both sides, being beaten with a stick (攵) — a rag worn to shreds.
radicals.notes: Used only in 幣 — ragged offerings of cloth 巾 hung at a shrine, later the paper money that replaced them.

radicals.meaning: respect, revere, defer to
radicals.story: A crouching figure 苟 beneath a raised stick 攵 — being made to bow low, the picture of showing respect.
radicals.notes: One of the 811. In 警 it gives the ケイ sound plus the sense of standing on one's guard.

radicals.meaning: written text, pattern, culture
radicals.story: A person standing face-on with a patterned, tattooed chest — those crossing decorative marks are the origin of 'writing'.
radicals.notes: 紋 'crest' preserves the original 'pattern' sense; in 対 the 文 is only a shinjitai stand-in for the left half of the old 對.

radicals.meaning: Aligned, uniform, all at one height.
radicals.story: Ears of grain drawn side by side and topped off at exactly the same height — dead level.
radicals.variant_notes: 斉 is the shinjitai of 齊, Kangxi radical 210.

radicals.meaning: a long-handled scoop used as a grain measure; the Big Dipper
radicals.story: A straight handle with two ticks marking the bowl — the standard scoop for measuring out grain, and the constellation named after it.
radicals.notes: 料 'fee, materials' is rice measured out by the dipper; 科 'course, department' is grain graded by it. Bigger than 勺 'ladle' and 匕 'spoon'.

radicals.meaning: axe, hatchet; cutting
radicals.story: A wedge-shaped axe head lashed to its haft, the blade jutting out to the left.
radicals.notes: It chops in 断 (cut off) and 新 (freshly cut timber). 質 stacks two axes on a shell.

radicals.meaning: cut off, behead, slash
radicals.story: A cart 車 beside an axe 斤 — the old execution rig that chops a body in two, so read it as a guillotine.
radicals.notes: Appears only in 暫, where it supplies the ザン reading.

radicals.meaning: a banner on a pole; direction, way, side
radicals.story: A crossbar lashed to a pole with a pennant trailing off the top — the standard people muster under in 旅 and 族, and by extension the direction it points.
radicals.notes: Real banner in 旅 (people under a flag = travel) and 族 (arrows under a flag = clan). Pure sound in 放 ホウ, 訪 ホウ, 房 ボウ. 方 vs 万: the banner has a dot and crossbar on top.

radicals.meaning: A child under a fluttering streamer; to roam.
radicals.story: A pole with a streamer flying off it (方 + 𠂉) and a child (子) underneath — a kid parading a flag through the streets.
radicals.notes: Used only in 遊.

radicals.meaning: A person turning away from the table, stuffed full.
radicals.story: A kneeling figure with the head twisted back and the mouth open — the diner who has had his fill and turns away.
radicals.notes: 既 pairs it with a food vessel: turning away from the bowl means you have already eaten.

radicals.meaning: sun; day, daytime, brightness
radicals.story: A box with one line through the middle — the sun was originally drawn as a circle with a dot inside, and the brush squared it off.
radicals.notes: 曰 (say-box) is wider and squatter, 目 (eye) is taller with two lines, 白 (white) has a flick on top, 田 (rice paddy) has a full cross.

radicals.meaning: daybreak, first light
radicals.story: The sun (日) resting on a single flat stroke — the horizon it has just cleared.
radicals.notes: Sun-on-horizon in 昼, pure sound タン in 担, and a worn-down shape in 量.

radicals.meaning: Old, former; the modern abbreviation of 舊.
radicals.story: One upright post standing beside a sun 日 — the shorthand block that replaced the complicated old form.
radicals.variant_notes: Inside 児 this shape does NOT mean 'old': it is the shinjitai replacement for 臼, the unfused skull-plates on an infant's head.

radicals.meaning: Bright, clear.
radicals.story: The sun (日) and the moon (月) set side by side — both lights burning at once.
radicals.notes: Used only in 盟 (an oath sworn in the bright light over a dish 皿 of blood — an alliance).

radicals.meaning: Twilight, nightfall.
radicals.story: The sun 日 tucked underneath a downward-hooking stroke — daylight sliding below the horizon.
radicals.notes: 婚 is woman + dusk because weddings were traditionally held at nightfall.

radicals.meaning: Long ago, the distant past.
radicals.story: Layer on layer of strokes piled above the sun 日 — days heaped on days until they are ancient history.

radicals.meaning: sunlight streaming down (the original of 陽)
radicals.story: The sun (日) resting on the horizon (一) with rays (勿) streaming away beneath it — light pouring off a rising sun.
radicals.notes: The classic trap: 易 'easy' puts 勿 straight under 日 with no horizon bar between them. 昜 has the extra bar.

radicals.meaning: this, this very one; right, correct
radicals.story: A sun 日 planted on a foot 龰 — the sun standing straight overhead at noon, pointing squarely at this very spot.
radicals.notes: Deliberately NOT keyworded 'correct' — that belongs to 正. Always 'noon sun': the sun with a foot under it, never bare 'sun' (日).

radicals.meaning: Warmth; a dish left in the sun.
radicals.story: A sun (日) sitting on a dish (皿) — a plate left out in the sunshine, warm to the touch.
radicals.variant_notes: The traditional form wrote 囚 (a prisoner) over 皿 — food given to a prisoner, hence kindness; Japanese writes 日.
radicals.notes: Used only in 温.

radicals.meaning: visible, manifest (Japanese form of 㬎)
radicals.story: Silk threads held up under the sun (日) to be inspected — the fine strands survive only as the stubby 业 shape beneath.
radicals.variant_notes: 㬎 is the full form: 日 over silk threads 絲 over the four dots 灬. Japanese collapses the threads and dots into the flat 业 of 显 (湿, 顕).
radicals.notes: In 顕 it supplies the meaning 'made visible'; in 湿 it is really a stand-in shape, though damp silk drying in the sun is a fair way to hold it.

radicals.meaning: bend, curve, warp; tune, melody, musical piece
radicals.story: A rectangle with two uprights ruled inside it, drawn as a bent bamboo container — anything bowed out of straight, and by extension a tune, which bends up and down.
radicals.notes: Indexed under Kangxi radical 73 (曰). The 'tune' sense (名曲, 作曲) is far more common in modern Japanese than the literal 'bend'.

radicals.meaning: One watch of the night; again, once more.
radicals.story: A sun 日 pinned under a bar with a long stroke sweeping away below — the day struck through and started over.
radicals.notes: The 'watch of the night' sense (夜が更ける) is chosen over the abstract 'again' so the keyword can be pictured.

radicals.meaning: To draw something out long; prolonged.
radicals.story: A cap (曰) over an eye (罒) with a hand (又) tugging from underneath — pulling something out long.
radicals.notes: Used only in 慢 (a heart stretched out — slow, and by extension slack or arrogant).

radicals.meaning: A stacked steaming pot; hence 'formerly' and the great- in great-grandparent.
radicals.story: Vapour (丷) rising off a lidded pot (田 over 日) — the old picture of a tiered rice steamer.
radicals.variant_notes: Shinjitai of 曾.
radicals.notes: Used only in 増 (earth piled up in tiers like the steamer's trays — increase).

radicals.meaning: moon; month — but see the note, since the identical shape often means flesh
radicals.story: A crescent hooked at the left with two strokes across the middle — the moon drawn as a sickle rather than a disc so it never gets mistaken for the sun 日.
radicals.variant_notes: ⺝ is written exactly like 月 but is a squashed 肉 'flesh'. Nothing in the strokes tells them apart — only the meaning of the whole character does.
radicals.notes: In 育, 胃, 背, 脅, 腹, 肩 this shape is FLESH, not the moon — if the character is about the body, read it as a slab of meat. 舟 (boat) also collapses toward this shape in 般, 船.

radicals.meaning: tree, wood, timber
radicals.story: A trunk running top to bottom with two branches lifting away and two roots spreading down — a tree seen from the side.
radicals.notes: Also sits at the bottom (条, 来, 楽) and inside enclosures (困). 本 is this tree with a mark at its root; 禾 is this tree with a drooping head.

radicals.meaning: a tree in a covered position; no independent meaning
radicals.story: 木 (tree) with its top bar tucked flush beneath whatever sits above it — a small tree squeezed under a cover.
radicals.variant_notes: 朩 is 木 as written when something is stacked directly on top of it (余, 茶, 雑); the strokes are the same, only the proportions compress.
radicals.notes: Add one dot to 朩 and you get 朮 (the component inside 術). Treat 'sapling' purely as a label for the covered position — it carries no meaning of its own.

radicals.meaning: not yet, unfinished, still to come
radicals.story: A tree 木 with an extra branch added near the top that is shorter than the one below it — the crown is still filling in, so the tree has not finished growing.
radicals.notes: 未 vs 末: in 未 the added top stroke is SHORTER than the branch below it (growth unfinished); in 末 (tip, end) it is LONGER, marking the very top of the tree. 妹 is the 'not yet grown' woman — a younger sister.

radicals.meaning: The very tip of a tree; the end, the last part.
radicals.story: A tree 木 with an extra-long bar drawn across its top to point straight at the topmost twig.
radicals.notes: The long stroke is on TOP (the tip); in 未 the long stroke is the lower one.

radicals.meaning: book; origin, root, main
radicals.story: A tree (木) with a short stroke ruled across its base, pointing at the root the whole tree grows out of.
radicals.notes: In 体 use its other sense — the root of a person is the body. 末 marks the treetop, 本 marks the root.

radicals.meaning: The glutinous millet plant.
radicals.story: A plant shaped like 木 with an extra grain hanging off its side — sticky millet.
radicals.notes: Sits in the middle of the crossroads 彳 + 亍 in 術.

radicals.meaning: A tree-shape with a dot flicked onto its upper branch.
radicals.story: The tree 木 with one extra dot added to the right arm — nothing more than that.
radicals.variant_notes: The same element as 朮 (a millet plant); Japanese printing places the dot on the arm inside 述 and 術.

radicals.meaning: A barb or spike on a branch.
radicals.story: A tree (木) with a barb swelling out of its trunk — a thorn branch.
radicals.notes: Used only in 策 (bamboo + thorn — the sharpened bamboo goad, later the bamboo slip you write a plan on).

radicals.meaning: bundle, bunch, sheaf; bind, tie up
radicals.story: A tree (木) with a band (口) cinched around its middle — firewood gathered and tied into a bundle.
radicals.notes: 束 vs 東: the box in 束 sits in the MIDDLE of the trunk (a band round the sticks); in 東 (east) it is the sun caught in the tree's branches, so the vertical runs right through a 日. This pair is a classic trap.

radicals.meaning: To come; next (as in next week).
radicals.story: A central stalk with ears drooping off both sides — originally a picture of a wheat plant, borrowed very early for the verb 'come'.

radicals.meaning: east, the direction of sunrise
radicals.story: The sun (日) caught in the branches of a tree (木) at dawn — the oldest forms are probably a sack tied at both ends, but the sunrise is the image worth keeping.
radicals.notes: 束 'bundle' has the box in the middle of the tree, 東 has the sun crossing it. The right half of 練 is historically 柬, not 東, though print shows the same shape.

radicals.meaning: grove, small stand of woods
radicals.story: Two trees (木) standing side by side — more than one tree, but not yet the three-tree forest 森.
radicals.notes: In 歴 this pair of trees is really a flattened 秝 (two grain plants); the shape was simplified into 林.

radicals.meaning: fruit; result, outcome
radicals.story: A tree 木 with a round fruit 田 sitting up in its crown.
radicals.notes: Differs from 東 (a sun 日 caught in the tree, not a fruit).

radicals.meaning: A thin flat piece — board, plate, leaf-blade.
radicals.story: 世 (three shoots sprouting off one line) set on a tree (木) — the thin flat slices you saw off a trunk.
radicals.notes: Same element under 蝶 (flat wings) and 諜 (flat writing tablet). Used only in 葉.

radicals.meaning: music; enjoyment, ease, comfort
radicals.story: A wooden frame 木 hung with a drum 白 and silk strings — a rack of instruments, hence music and the ease it brings.
radicals.notes: One of the 811. For 薬 the useful half is the ラク 'ease, comfort' sense: the grass that makes you comfortable again.

radicals.meaning: yawn, open mouth; lack, be missing
radicals.story: A kneeling figure with its mouth cranked wide open — the original picture of a yawn, which is why it stands beside 飲 (drink), 歌 (sing) and 欲 (crave).
radicals.notes: Always the right-hand element. As a kanji on its own it means 'lack' (欠ける), but the mouth image is what drives every compound in this set.

radicals.meaning: The one after; order, rank.
radicals.story: Two short strokes (冫) beside a person with their mouth wide open (欠) — the one yawning in line, waiting their turn.
radicals.notes: Used only in 資 (the next shells in the pile — capital, resources).

radicals.meaning: a planted foot; to stop, to halt
radicals.story: A left foot pressed into the ground with the toes at the top and the heel at the bottom — a foot planted has stopped moving, which is how it came to mean 'stop'.
radicals.variant_notes: 止 sits on top or on the left; 龰 is the squashed form that carries the bottom of 走 and 足.
radicals.notes: Whenever you see it, someone is walking or has just stopped: 歩 (two feet), 歴 (footprints through history), 企 (a person up on tiptoe).

radicals.meaning: correct, proper, straight, exact
radicals.story: A foot (止) planted directly under the line (一) it is marching at — head straight for the mark without wavering and you are correct.
radicals.notes: 正 is 止 (stop/footprint) with one extra bar on top. Both セイ and ショウ readings are live and both get passed to derivatives (政セイ, 証ショウ).

radicals.meaning: To walk, to step, to go on foot.
radicals.story: One footprint 止 planted, and a second one stepping out below it — left, then right.
radicals.notes: 渉 is water plus footsteps — crossing on foot — a meaning compound rather than a sound compound.

radicals.meaning: bare bones, death, decay
radicals.story: A stripped and cracked bone: the two short strokes on top are the splintered end, the rest is the shaft.
radicals.variant_notes: 歺 is the older printed form with an extra stroke at the top; identical in use.
radicals.notes: 歹 is 夕 with a bar ruled across the top.

radicals.meaning: a pole weapon wielded in the hand; striking, action done by force
radicals.story: A right hand (又) at the base gripping the shaft of a long bamboo club raised above it.
radicals.notes: Always on the right; the 又 at its foot is the hand doing the hitting, which is why 投 means throw and 段 a step beaten out.

radicals.meaning: do not, must not; the shinjitai stand-in for 母 inside 毎 and 毒
radicals.story: 母 with its two dots run together into a single long bar — a mother with her arm barred across the doorway saying 'don't'.
radicals.variant_notes: 母 keeps the two dots and is the standalone kanji for mother; 毋 merges them into one bar and is the form that appears inside 毎 and 毒.
radicals.notes: Kangxi files 母 under this radical, so the two are officially one family.

radicals.meaning: Mother.
radicals.story: A kneeling woman drawn with two dots for her breasts — the nursing mother.

radicals.meaning: Every, each time.
radicals.story: A mother 母 with a hair-ornament stroke laid across the top — the old picture of a woman, borrowed long ago for 'every'.

radicals.meaning: compare, line up against, ratio
radicals.story: Two people in the same crouched pose (匕匕) standing one behind the other so you can size them up against each other.
radicals.notes: 北 is these same two people turned back-to-back; in 皆 比 is meaning only, though it lends ヒ elsewhere (批).

radicals.meaning: clan, family name; Mr./Ms. as a formal suffix
radicals.story: The graphic origin is genuinely disputed, so read the shape as it looks: a banner hanging from a slanted pole, the standard a family marches behind.
radicals.notes: In 紙 it is pure sound (シ) — do not read 'clan' into paper. Add one stroke underneath and you get 氐, the element in 低・底.

radicals.meaning: base, foundation, the lowest part
radicals.story: The clan blade 氏 with an extra stroke ruled underneath it — a line marking the very bottom that everything else rests on.
radicals.notes: A dependable sound tag: 低 テイ, 底 テイ.

radicals.meaning: the people, populace, civilian
radicals.story: Usually explained as an eye with a spike driven through it — a blinded captive, and so the common folk living under someone else's rule.
radicals.notes: Deliberately kept distinct from 人 'person': 民 is the governed populace. 氏 is the same shape without the extra stroke.

radicals.meaning: vapour, air, breath
radicals.story: Layered wisps drifting sideways and curling up at the tail — vapour rising off something hot.
radicals.notes: In 気 it wraps the top and right around 㐅; the traditional form 氣 held 米 'rice' inside instead — steam off cooking rice. Not 乞 'beg', which ends in a 乙 hook with no third wisp.

radicals.meaning: water
radicals.story: A central current with spray flying off to either side — a stream in motion.
radicals.variant_notes: 氵 (three drops) is the left-hand form; 氺 is the flattened bottom form (求, 泰); 水 stands alone or sits whole inside a kanji.
radicals.notes: 氷 is 水 plus one ice-dot; 永 is 水 with a lid stroke on top.

radicals.meaning: water; liquid, wet, flowing — anything to do with rivers, washing, or fluid
radicals.story: Three short flicks stacked down the left edge — two drops and a splash, water shaken off a hand; it is 水 squeezed sideways so the rest of the character can share the square.
radicals.variant_notes: 水 is the free-standing kanji; 氵 (さんずい) is the left-side form; 氺 is the rare bottom form (as in 泰). Same primitive, three postures.
radicals.notes: Parent is 水. Count the flicks: 氵 has three, 冫 (ice) has two, 忄 (heart) has two flanking a vertical.

radicals.meaning: Water that never runs dry; forever.
radicals.story: A single drop 丶 riding on a water-like flow — a river drawn with its tributaries, so long it has no end.

radicals.meaning: The water element flattened to sit underneath.
radicals.story: Water 水 squashed until its side strokes splay out level — a splash spreading beneath whatever sits above it.
radicals.variant_notes: A positional variant OF water, not an independent primitive; keyworded separately only so 求 has something to name.

radicals.meaning: seek, request, demand
radicals.story: The old form drew a fur robe with pelt-hairs bristling out on both sides — the sense 'seek' is a later sound-borrowing — so read the strokes instead as an arm thrust out over splayed hairs, a palm held open to beg.
radicals.notes: In 救 and 球 it lends only the sound キュウ — do not look for 'seeking' in their meanings. The lower half is 氺, the stretched form of 水.

radicals.meaning: spring, wellspring, source of water
radicals.story: White 白 water 水 — clear water bubbling up out of the ground as a natural spring.
radicals.notes: Keyworded 'fountain' rather than 'spring' to avoid clashing with the season; 原 is this same spring tucked under a cliff.

radicals.meaning: The Luo River in China, past the old capital Luoyang.
radicals.story: Water (氵) beside 各 — no picture here, only a proper name, so see a river with a name-board planted beside it.
radicals.notes: Honest label: it is a place name doing sound duty. Used only in 落 (leaves dropping into the Luo).

radicals.meaning: fire, flame, burning
radicals.story: A central flame with a spark flying off each side — a bonfire seen head-on.
radicals.variant_notes: 灬 is the four-dot bottom form, the embers under a pot (点, 熱, 無); 火 keeps its full shape standing alone and on the left (炉, 焼).
radicals.notes: 秋 'autumn' is grain (禾) plus fire — burning off the stubble after harvest.

radicals.meaning: fire; the four-dot form of 火 that sits under a character
radicals.story: Four short flames flicking upward from underneath — the fire 火 flattened out beneath a pot; be warned that the identical four dots under 馬 and 鳥 are really the animal's legs and tail feathers, not fire.
radicals.variant_notes: 火 stands alone or sits on the left (炉, 秋); 灬 is the four-dot form used only across the bottom.
radicals.notes: Real fire in 点, 黒, 熱, 無, 然; borrowed shape in 馬 and 鳥.

radicals.meaning: Ash; the cold leavings of a fire.
radicals.story: A fire 火 sheltering under the sweeping stroke 厂 — what you can finally rake out by hand once the flames are dead.

radicals.meaning: flame, blaze, inflammation
radicals.story: Fire 火 stacked on fire 火 — flames climbing in two tiers.
radicals.notes: Deliberately 'blaze' so it never collides with 火 'fire'; in 談 it gives both the sound and the sense of talking heatedly by the fire.

radicals.meaning: A flame being put out.
radicals.story: A fire (火) trapped inside the arms of 戌 — flame snuffed out under a blade.
radicals.notes: Used only in 滅.

radicals.meaning: claw, a hand grasping from above
radicals.story: A hand reaching down from above with the fingers curled under — 爪 (claw) squashed flat so it can sit on a character's roof.
radicals.variant_notes: 爪 is the full standing form used alone or at the bottom; 爫 is the flattened top form (受, 愛); ⺤ is a font variant of that same top form.
radicals.notes: In 受 the claw hands something DOWN to the 又 (right hand) waiting below — a hand-off, which is exactly 'receive'.

radicals.meaning: to pull, to draw out (the original of 援)
radicals.story: A hand reaching down from above (爫) and another hand below (又), both gripping the same bar across the middle — two people hauling on one object.
radicals.notes: Like 受 it opens with the downward claw-hand 爫; 爰 has the bar and lower hand instead of 冖.

radicals.meaning: father
radicals.story: A hand gripping a stone axe — the upper strokes are the raised arm, the crossing strokes below the axe itself, the tool of the man who feeds the household.
radicals.notes: Sits on top in 爺 and 釜, but at the bottom in 交. Not 文 'writing', whose upper strokes are a lid 亠, not an arm.

radicals.meaning: one of a pair, one side; a scrap, a fragment
radicals.story: Split a tree (木) straight down the middle and keep the right-hand piece — that half-plank is 片, hence both 'one side of a pair' and 'a chip broken off'.
radicals.notes: The mirror-image left half of the same split tree is 爿 (short form 丬, seen in 状, 将, 寝) — a different primitive, not a variant of this one.

radicals.meaning: cow, ox, cattle
radicals.story: A cow's head seen straight on — the horns are the top slash and the crossbar, the long vertical runs down its face.
radicals.variant_notes: 牛 stands alone or sits inside (解, 制); on the left (物, 特, 件) the bottom horizontal lifts into a rising stroke, written 牜.
radicals.notes: 牛 vs 午: the cow's top slash sits left of the vertical and the vertical pokes above the upper bar; in 午 (noon) it does not.

radicals.meaning: dog
radicals.story: 大 'big' with one small extra stroke for the pricked ear — a big animal with something sticking out of it.
radicals.variant_notes: 犭 is the compressed left-hand form used before another element (独, 猛); 犬 keeps its full shape standing alone or on the right/bottom (状, 然, 伏).
radicals.notes: 然 originally meant 'to burn' — dog flesh (⺝ + 犬) over a fire (灬).

radicals.meaning: beast, animal — the left-hand form of 犬
radicals.story: 犬 'dog' stood up on its hind legs and squeezed against the left edge — a lean beast in profile.
radicals.variant_notes: 犬 is the free-standing form and the right/bottom form; 犭 is the narrow left-hand form used before another element.
radicals.notes: 独 'alone' is a single beast with one bug (虫); 猛 'fierce' is a savage one. Against 彳: 犭 has a curved belly stroke, 彳 is all straight slants.

radicals.meaning: deep black, dark, mysterious, profound
radicals.story: A lid (亠) over a small skein of silk (幺) — thread dropped into the dye vat and lifted out a deep, unreadable black.
radicals.notes: Heisig and WaniKani use 'mysterious'; 'dark thread' keeps it picturable while preserving the darkness sense. Lends ゲン in 弦・舷, outside this set.

radicals.meaning: jewel, jade, ball, gem
radicals.story: Three jade discs strung on one cord (王) with a single extra bead dotted in at the side — that dot is all that separates the jewel from 王 the king.
radicals.variant_notes: On the left 玉 drops its dot and is written ⺩, indistinguishable from 王 (king) — which is why 理・珍・球・現 are jade words, not king words.
radicals.notes: In 国 the jewel is the treasure sealed inside the national borders.

radicals.meaning: king, ruler; but on the left of a character it is jade
radicals.story: Three horizontal lines skewered by a single vertical, traditionally read as heaven, humanity and earth held together by the one who rules them — though the older origin is likely a broad axe-head, the badge of authority.
radicals.variant_notes: 玉 'jade' keeps its dot when standing alone; on the left of a character the dot is dropped and it is written identically to 王 (⺩, おうへん).
radicals.notes: IMPORTANT: in 珍, 現, 球, 理 this element is JADE, not a king. Use 'king' only where the character is genuinely about rule. In 全 and 金 it is neither — it is the remains of a different old shape.

radicals.meaning: sweet; indulgent, naive
radicals.story: A mouth (口) with a short stroke laid inside it, marking the exact spot on the tongue where something delicious is being held.
radicals.notes: Wider and flatter than 日, with the two side strokes poking below the base; 廿 'twenty' has no stroke inside it.

radicals.meaning: life, birth, be born; raw, fresh; student
radicals.story: A seedling putting out its first leaf above the ground line — something pushing up out of the soil.
radicals.notes: 生 vs 牛: 牛 (cow) has only two crossbars and its top stroke slants; 生 has three bars, the middle one longest. This kanji has an unusually wide reading spread (なま, いきる, うまれる, セイ, ショウ).

radicals.meaning: use, employ; business, errand
radicals.story: Its origin is unsettled, so take the shape at face value: a slatted wooden pail with a handle laid across the middle and one leg poking out below.
radicals.notes: Meaning is the abstract 'use'; the bucket is the picture that makes it stick. 甬 (通・痛) is this same bucket with a lid on top.

radicals.meaning: a hollow tube that things pass through
radicals.story: A spout (龴) fitted to the top of 用 — the true origin is disputed (most often a bell with a loop handle), so take the shape at face value as a container with a pipe out the top that everything in this family bursts or flows through.
radicals.notes: 通 'pass through' is the pipe plus a road (辶); 痛 'pain' is sickness (疒) shooting down that pipe. 用 'use' is the same shape without the spout.

radicals.meaning: cultivated field, rice paddy
radicals.story: A square divided by a cross into four equal plots — a paddy seen from above, with the irrigation paths running between the fields.
radicals.notes: The 田/由/申/甲 cluster is the single worst lookalike set in the language: 由 pokes out the top, 甲 out the bottom, 申 out both ends, 田 out neither. In 思, 累, 略 the 田 is a field; in 胃 and 界 it is not always.

radicals.meaning: reason, cause, origin; via, by way of; freedom (自由)
radicals.story: A squat vessel (田) with a narrow spout pushing up out of the top — the jar the contents come from, hence 'where a thing comes from'; the true origin is disputed.
radicals.notes: The 田/由/申/甲 quartet is the single worst lookalike cluster for beginners: 由 pokes out the TOP, 甲 out the BOTTOM, 申 out BOTH ends, 田 neither. As a kanji it means 理由 'reason' — the jar is the mnemonic peg for that 'origin' sense. Within these 811 it never actually carries its sound (届 and 画 are simplification artifacts).

radicals.meaning: a plate of armor, a hard shell; first in a series
radicals.story: A panel (田) with a single strap hanging straight down from it — one plate of scale armor tied in place.
radicals.notes: The look-alikes differ only in which way the stroke breaks out of 田: 甲 downward, 由 upward, 申 both ways. 押 'push' shows the コウ→オウ sound shift; in 単 the 甲 is only a shape.

radicals.meaning: say humbly, report; (originally) lightning
radicals.story: A bolt striking down through the clouds — the ancient zigzag has been straightened into a line driven clean through a box.
radicals.notes: 申 pokes out top and bottom, 甲 only below, 由 only above. The kanji means 'say humbly' (申す), but the lightning drives 神 (altar + lightning = god).

radicals.meaning: full, brimming; a filled storage vessel
radicals.story: A lid (一) on a wide mouth (口) above a packed field (田) — a squat storehouse filled to the brim, drawn in the old script as a bulging jar.
radicals.notes: Its 'full' sense feeds 富 (wealth) and 福 (blessing); in 幅 it is mostly sound.

radicals.meaning: one's turn; number in a series; to keep watch
radicals.story: A beast's paw print (釆) pressed across a field (田) — the same round trodden night after night, hence taking turns and standing watch.
radicals.notes: Under the roof in 審, on the left in 翻. The watch sense survives in 交番 (police box) and 番人 (watchman).

radicals.meaning: different, strange, unusual
radicals.story: A 田 raised up on two hands 共 — commonly read as a person holding a mask (or a winnowing basket) over the face, a strange sight.
radicals.notes: Its dictionary sense is 'different'; 'masked figure' is used as the keyword because it is imageable and makes 翼 work — feathers 羽 spread above a costumed dancer. The mask account is the common one but not certain, hence the hedge in the story.

radicals.meaning: doubt, suspect, be unsure
radicals.story: Traditionally read as a person leaning on a staff halting at a fork in the road, head turned, unable to decide which way to go.
radicals.notes: Abstract keyword, but it is the component's own core sense (Heisig/WaniKani agree); the halted-traveller image in the story is what 凝 'congeal, frozen in place' should compose with.

radicals.meaning: illness, disease, the sickroom
radicals.story: A bed (爿) tipped on its side under a roof stroke with the patient laid out on it — the sickroom that every illness kanji is filed under.
radicals.notes: Usually glossed just 'sickness'; 'sickbed' keeps the picture (it is literally the 爿 bed of 丬). Distinguish from 广 (lean-to), which has no dots on the left edge.

radicals.meaning: two feet turned outward, stepping up
radicals.story: A left foot and a right foot turned away from each other — the splayed stance of someone stepping up onto something.
radicals.notes: 登 'climb' puts those feet above a ritual stand (豆); 発 'depart, emit' sends them off — its ハツ reading echoes 癶's own.

radicals.meaning: To set out, launch, emit, issue forth.
radicals.story: 癶, a pair of feet splayed toe-out, planted above a squashed-down bow-and-hand — the instant of pushing off and setting out.
radicals.variant_notes: Shinjitai squash of 發, whose lower half was 弓 + 殳.
radicals.notes: Used only in 廃 (a shelter everyone has departed from, hence abolished).

radicals.meaning: white; pale, plain, clear, blank
radicals.story: A sun 日 with a small flick rising off its top — the first pale ray of dawn washing the sky white (the true origin is disputed; the shape may be a thumbnail or a grain of rice).
radicals.notes: Lends ハク in 泊 and 迫, ヒャク in 百. Against 日 (sun) and 自 (nose): 白 has a short flick on top, 自 has a full horizontal shoulder.

radicals.meaning: One hundred.
radicals.story: A single stroke 一 laid across the top of 白 — add one more and the count tops out at a hundred.
radicals.notes: In 宿 this shape is a worn-down sleeping mat, not the number — a person 亻 lying on a mat under a roof 宀 is a lodging. Use the number only as a shape cue there.

radicals.meaning: skin, hide, leather, bark
radicals.story: A hand (又) at the bottom pulling the flap of hide up and off the carcass above it.
radicals.notes: In 彼疲破 it carries only the sound ヒ/ハ — the skin meaning does not come through.

radicals.meaning: dish, shallow bowl, plate
radicals.story: A footed bowl seen from the side, the two inner strokes its dividers and the base line the table it stands on.
radicals.notes: 血 is this same dish with one drop added on top.

radicals.meaning: eye; seeing, looking, watching
radicals.story: A tall box with two lines inside — an eye stood on end so it fits the square, the bars being the pupil and the fold of the lid.
radicals.notes: 日 (sun) is shorter with one line; 自 (nose/self) is 目 with a flick on top; 且 has a foot sticking out at the bottom.

radicals.meaning: Straight, direct, upright.
radicals.story: Ten 十 eyes 目 sighting down one line, with a bent rule 𠃊 laid underneath to prove it runs true.

radicals.meaning: Facing each other; mutual, and by extension appearance or minister.
radicals.story: An eye (目) set right beside a tree (木), each sizing up the other — two things face to face.
radicals.notes: Used only in 想 (two hearts facing each other — holding a thought).

radicals.meaning: true, genuine, real, exact
radicals.story: A ladle 匕 above 具, goods held up on a stand — the origin is disputed, so read it as inspecting the goods to confirm they are genuine.
radicals.notes: One of the 811. No oracle-bone story invented — the two competing accounts (a person + a cauldron; an inverted figure) are both unsettled.

radicals.meaning: halberd, pike, thrusting spear
radicals.story: A long shaft running down the character with a blade and a dangling tassel crossing it near the top — the pictograph of a bladed polearm.
radicals.notes: Deliberately split from 戈: 矛 is the spear you thrust, 戈 is the axe blade bolted sideways. Reliable ム sound in 務.

radicals.meaning: arrow, dart
radicals.story: A shaft with the barbed head at the top and the flights spreading at the bottom — an arrow drawn side-on.
radicals.notes: 矢 vs 失: the arrow's top stroke is a short flat bar; 失 (lose) has that stroke pushed out to the left as a slash. This pair trips up almost every learner.

radicals.meaning: stone, rock
radicals.story: A boulder (口) that has tumbled out from under a rock overhang (丆).
radicals.notes: 石 has the flat-topped 丆; 右 has the sweeping 𠂇 — the difference is which way the top stroke leans.

radicals.meaning: altar, offering table; to show, to reveal
radicals.story: A flat stone table standing on two legs with the offering dripping down between them — the altar where sacrifices are set out for the gods.
radicals.variant_notes: 示 sits at the bottom or stands whole (宗・祭・禁); on the left it compresses to the four-stroke 礻 (社・神・礼・祝). 礻 has one dot fewer than 衤 (clothing, from 衣) — the classic mix-up.
radicals.notes: Every 礻 kanji is about gods, shrines and ritual — the altar is the giveaway. In 宗 it is semantic; it only lends シ outside this 811 set (視).

radicals.meaning: altar, the gods, the sacred; the left-hand form of 示
radicals.story: The altar 示 squeezed narrow so it can stand on the left — an offering table with the streamers of the gods hanging down from it.
radicals.variant_notes: 示 is the full form, standing alone or sitting at the bottom (宗, 祭); 礻 is the four-stroke compressed form used only on the left (礼, 社, 祝, 神).
radicals.notes: The single biggest radical mix-up in the language: 礻 (4 strokes, one dot before the hook) is sacred — 神, 社, 礼, 祝. 衤 (5 strokes, an extra dot lower down) is cloth — 初, 複, 裕. Check the dot count.

radicals.meaning: festival, religious rite, offering
radicals.story: A hand (又) laying a slab of meat (⺼) onto an altar table (示) — the offering that opens a festival.
radicals.notes: Sits under the roof in 察 and on the right in 際. Every part of it is a real thing: hand, meat, altar.

radicals.meaning: A long-tailed monkey (the traditional gloss for this shape).
radicals.story: A boxy head 田 above a body with a curled tail hanging off it — traditionally read as a long-tailed monkey.
radicals.notes: Keep it apart from any 'monkey' keyword used for 申 — 禺 is the ape with the tail.

radicals.meaning: cereal plant, grain, rice in the field
radicals.story: A tree 木 with an extra stroke drooping off the top — a grain plant bent over by the weight of its own ripe head.
radicals.notes: Called のぎへん. Grain meant food and food meant taxes, which is why it shows up in 利, 私, 税, 秋, 科.

radicals.meaning: A crop in full ear; outstanding, excelling.
radicals.story: A grain plant (禾) with its head bending over (乃) — the crop in full ear, standing out above the rest.
radicals.notes: Used only in 誘 (words in full bloom — sweet-talking someone into it).

radicals.meaning: cave, hole, cavity, opening; pit dwelling
radicals.story: A roof (宀) with the ground split open (八) beneath it — a dwelling dug back into a hillside.
radicals.notes: 穴 vs 六: 六 (six) has a flat 亠 lid with no side strokes; 穴 has the full 宀 roof with its left-hand drop. Kept as 'cave' rather than 'hole' so it stays distinct from 凵 (pit).

radicals.meaning: stand, stand up; establish, set up
radicals.story: A figure with arms spread and legs planted, drawn on top of the ground line beneath it — a person standing their ground.
radicals.notes: 立 vs 辛: 辛 (bitter) is 立 with an extra cross below. Note the transitive/intransitive pair the kanji writes: 立つ (stand, intr.) / 立てる (set up, tr.).

radicals.meaning: to contend, to vie, to race
radicals.story: A figure standing tall (立) above a wide-open mouth (兄) — someone squaring up and shouting a challenge; 競 simply sets two of them side by side for the race.
radicals.variant_notes: 竸 is an old variant of 競 built from two 言-topped contenders; modern Japanese uses 競, two plain 竞.
radicals.notes: Not 竟 'after all': 竟 is 立 over 兄 too but is a single character in its own right, used in 境 and 鏡.

radicals.meaning: The end of a piece; a limit, a boundary.
radicals.story: A sound (音) standing on a pair of legs (儿) — the moment the music stops and the player walks off, the end of the piece.
radicals.notes: Used only in 境 (the finish line drawn on the ground 土 — a border).

radicals.meaning: bamboo; by extension writing implements, baskets, and anything woven from it
radicals.story: Two identical stalks standing side by side, each a short stem with a leaf drooping off it — a small stand of bamboo.
radicals.variant_notes: ⺮ (たけかんむり) is the flattened top form used in every character here — 笑, 第, 等, 答, 算. Same six strokes, just squashed.
radicals.notes: Bamboo strips were the writing surface before paper, which is why it tops 筆, 第, 等, 算, 節. Against 艹 (flowers): bamboo has two separate hooked stalks, grass has one continuous bar.

radicals.meaning: husked rice; grains of rice
radicals.story: Grains of husked rice flying off a central stalk in all four directions — a cross with a dot flung into each quadrant.
radicals.notes: Genuine rice in 料, 粗, 粘, 精, 類. In 断, 歯 and 奥 the 米 shape is a stroke collision, not rice.

radicals.meaning: thread, silk, string; binding, weaving, continuity
radicals.story: A twisted coil at the top over three loose ends hanging below — a spool of silk with its fibres dangling.
radicals.variant_notes: 糹 is the compressed left-side form (いとへん); in Japanese type it is usually still printed as 糸. Same primitive.
radicals.notes: 系 is this thread with an extra flick on top (a hand lifting the skein). 幺 is just the coil, no dangling ends.

radicals.meaning: Threads gathered at the top and hanging in one line.
radicals.story: A single stroke hooks over the thread 糸 and holds it up, so everything below hangs from that one point.

radicals.meaning: to measure a girth with a cord; tidy, unsoiled
radicals.story: A notched tally 㓞 above a thread 糸 — a cord wound around something and knotted tight to take its measure.
radicals.notes: Carries both the ケツ sound and the 'trim and clean' sense into 潔.

radicals.meaning: to suspend, hang up; (later borrowed for) county, prefecture
radicals.story: A head 県 — drawn upside-down — knotted to a cord 系, a head strung up for display.
radicals.variant_notes: 県 is the modern short form and one of the 811 in its own right ('prefecture'); the full 縣 with its cord survives only inside 懸.
radicals.notes: Two words on purpose so it never reads as plain 頁 'head'. 懸 = hanging head + heart 心, i.e. left hanging, at stake.

radicals.meaning: net, snare
radicals.story: A net stretched on its frame with the mesh knots showing — laid flat across the top of a kanji it ends up looking like 目 'eye' tipped on its side.
radicals.variant_notes: 网 is the full standalone character; 罒 is the flattened form used across the top of a kanji (買, 罰, 置, 罪); 罓 and 㓁 are older printed variants.
radicals.notes: Not 四 'four': 四 is closed at the bottom and its inner strokes splay outward. In 買 it is the net you haul cowries home in.

radicals.meaning: The deep inside of a hole.
radicals.story: A hole pinched shut at the top with something reaching down into it — the far end of a burrow.
radicals.notes: The same element gives 深 'deep'; with a hand 扌 in front you are groping down the burrow, which is 探 'search'.

radicals.meaning: sheep, ram
radicals.story: Two curling horns over a head and body seen straight on — a ram facing you.
radicals.variant_notes: 𦍌 and ⺷ are the docked top forms used as a cap (美, 着, 差, 義); 羊 keeps its tail stroke when it stands alone or sits on the right (洋, 様).
radicals.notes: 洋 'ocean, Western' is water + sheep for the ヨウ sound; in 遅 'late' the 羊 is a postwar squash of 犀 'rhinoceros', not a real sheep.

radicals.meaning: righteousness, justice, proper duty; meaning; in-law
radicals.story: A sheep 羊 raised above a jagged blade 我 — the flawless ram offered up, the old image of doing what is right.
radicals.notes: One of the 811. 議 is words 言 + righteousness: arguing over what is right.

radicals.meaning: feathers, wings, plumage
radicals.story: Two wings side by side, each drawn as a curved quill with the barbs ticked in.
radicals.notes: The doubled element in 弱 looks like feathers but is 弓 + 冫 twice.

radicals.meaning: long-tailed pheasant
radicals.story: Long feathers (羽) spread above a short-tailed bird (隹) — a pheasant seen from overhead, all plumage.
radicals.notes: 曜 ヨウ, 躍 ヤク, 濯 タク — the same bird, three readings. A pheasant bursting upward makes 躍 'leap' easy to hold.

radicals.meaning: old age, an elder
radicals.story: A stooped elder: the long stroke sweeping down to the left is his bent back and cane, the crossed strokes above are his straggling hair.
radicals.variant_notes: 老 is the full standalone character (this top plus 匕); 耂 is the top-left radical form used in 考 and 者.
radicals.notes: Do not read the top as 土 (soil) — the long sweep down the left is the giveaway.

radicals.meaning: person, one who does X (agent suffix)
radicals.story: An elder (耂) standing over a sun-box (日); the graphic origin is genuinely disputed, so read it as a nameless figure — the someone who does whatever the other half names.
radicals.notes: Keyword is 'someone', kept deliberately distinct from 人 'person' and 亻. Older print forms add a 丶 above the 日; the Japanese standard form (8 strokes) has none.

radicals.meaning: beard, whiskers (original picture); classical 'and, moreover'
radicals.story: A chin line drawn across the top with four whiskers hanging down beneath the jaw — a beard.
radicals.notes: Honest label: in modern compounds (需・耐) 而 carries neither a reliable meaning nor a reliable sound, so learn it as the beard shape and move on.

radicals.meaning: A young plant shown tip and root; the beginning, the tip.
radicals.story: A shoot pushing up at the top over 而, the rootlets hanging below the soil line — one plant drawn from tip to root.
radicals.notes: Called 'seedling' not 'sprout' so it stays distinct from 屮. Used only in 端.

radicals.meaning: ear
radicals.story: The outer rim, the inner ridges and the hanging lobe of a human ear seen in profile.
radicals.notes: 耳 vs 目: the ear's two verticals stick out above and below the box; the eye 目 is a sealed rectangle.

radicals.meaning: a hand gripping an upright writing brush
radicals.story: A fist closed around an upright brush with the ruled lines of the strokes it lays down — this is the original character behind 筆 'writing brush'.
radicals.variant_notes: ⺻ is the reduced form used as a cap (書 and its family); 聿 keeps its full shape on the right (律, 建).
radicals.notes: 律 'law' is what the brush writes down and the foot (彳) then walks; 建 'build' is the plan brushed out and set striding (廴).

radicals.meaning: meat, flesh; the body
radicals.story: The outer frame is the cut edge of a slab and the two 人-shaped strokes inside are the streaks of marbling running through it — a piece of meat seen in cross-section.
radicals.variant_notes: Squeezed into ⺼/⺝ when it becomes a body-part radical, sitting on the left (肌・腕) or underneath (背・胃); in Japanese fonts that form is printed identically to 月 moon.
radicals.notes: This app's decomposition lists the flesh radical as 月, so read 'moon' on a body-part kanji (育・胃・背・脅) as meat.

radicals.meaning: A small piece pared off; to resemble in miniature.
radicals.story: Small 小 sitting on a slab of flesh ⺝ — a thin sliver shaved off the meat.
radicals.notes: The 'pared down to nothing' sense drives 消 (extinguish) and 削 (shave).

radicals.meaning: To bring up, nurture, rear.
radicals.story: A child drawn upside-down (𠫓, head-first out of the womb) above a body (月) — a newborn being brought up.
radicals.notes: Used only in 徹, where 育 is a shinjitai stand-in for 鬲 (a cauldron) and carries neither meaning nor sound — treat any 'raise' mnemonic there as a hook, not an etymology.

radicals.meaning: The bearded northern nomads (胡人); originally the dewlap under an animal's jaw.
radicals.story: Old (古) flesh (月) — the sagging dewlap hanging under a chin, a graph later used for the bearded northerners the Chinese called Hu.
radicals.notes: Used only in 湖.

radicals.meaning: minister, retainer, vassal, subject
radicals.story: An eye stood on end and drawn wide open — the staring eye of a servant kneeling with his head bowed before his lord.
radicals.notes: Nearly identical to 巨 (huge) — check which side the middle strokes hook toward. In 監 the minister leans over a dish of water to look at his reflection.

radicals.meaning: nose; self, oneself, from
radicals.story: A pictograph of a nose seen head-on — the bridge across the top, the nostril lines ruled inside — and Japanese speakers still point at their own nose to mean 'me', which is how it came to write 'self'.
radicals.notes: Keyword is 'nose', not 'self', because the nose is what makes 息 (breath = nose + heart), 鼻 (nose) and 首 (head) readable. The kanji itself still means 自分 'oneself'.

radicals.meaning: an arrow that has struck the ground; to arrive, to reach the limit
radicals.story: An arrow drawn point-down with the ground ruled beneath it — the shaft has landed, so it has arrived.
radicals.notes: 室 'room' is the innermost place the arrow finally reaches under a roof (宀); 屋 'roof, shop' puts the same arrival under 尸.

radicals.meaning: tongue
radicals.story: A forked tongue (the 千-like top) poking out of an open mouth (口) below.
radicals.notes: In 活 the 舌 shape is a modern merger of a different old element; picture a tongue anyway.

radicals.meaning: feet pointing opposite ways; contrary, discordant, error
radicals.story: Two footprints side by side at the foot of the character, the left one turned left and the right one turned right — feet splayed in opposite directions.
radicals.notes: Its only appearance in this set is 舞 (dance), where splayed feet are exactly the point. The left half is easy to misread as 夕 (evening).

radicals.meaning: a small boat, a hull
radicals.story: A narrow hull with a plank bench across the middle and a bow stroke on top — a dugout canoe seen from above.
radicals.notes: 般 'sort, carry' is a boat plus a hand-weapon (殳) poling it along; 船 'ship' is the hull plus 㕣 for the sound.

radicals.meaning: to stop and glare back; stubbornness
radicals.story: An eye (the boxed top) over a body twisting round beneath it — someone who has stopped dead and is glaring back over the shoulder.
radicals.notes: 艮 vs 良: 良 (good) has an extra dot or stroke on top. In 退, 限, 根 and 銀 the 艮 is carrying sound, not the glare.

radicals.meaning: good, fine, superior
radicals.story: The graphic origin is disputed, so read the shape plainly: a funnel with a dot of grain going in at the top, a sieve in the middle, and the good grain spilling out below.
radicals.notes: Textbooks gloss the kanji itself simply as 'good'; the grain image is kept so 食 (person + choice grain = eat) composes.

radicals.meaning: color; also sensuality, lust
radicals.story: A bent-over figure (𠂊) leaning across a kneeling one (巴) — the flush that rises in the skin, which is why 色 covers both 'color' and 'lust'.
radicals.notes: The sensual sense is live in modern Japanese (色っぽい, 色気), so the two-people reading is worth keeping.

radicals.meaning: grass, plants, herbs — any growing green thing
radicals.story: Two little sprouts standing side by side, clipped down to one crossbar with two stems poking through — a strip of vegetation laid across the top of the character.
radicals.variant_notes: 艸 is the full ancient form (two 屮 sprouts, 6 strokes); modern Japanese writes 艹 as 3 strokes with one unbroken bar, while traditional printing splits the bar into 4 strokes (⺿).
radicals.notes: Called くさかんむり. Against 竹 on top (たけかんむり): grass is one flat bar, bamboo is two separate hooked stalks.

radicals.meaning: As a character, 'carelessly, if only'; graphically just grass over a phrase.
radicals.story: Grass (艹) growing over a phrase (句); the character has no vivid picture behind it, so read the shape literally as weeds sprouting out of some words.
radicals.notes: Honest shape keyword — the traditional readings of 苟 in 敬 are disputed and not worth inventing. Used only in 敬.

radicals.meaning: a bundle of undergrowth; menial labour
radicals.story: A thicket of upright shoots (丵) gripped from below by two hands (廾) — an armful of brushwood, the sort of load a servant is sent to haul.
radicals.notes: Not 業: 業 finishes with 木 at the bottom, 菐 finishes with the two lifting hands.

radicals.meaning: to seize a bird by hand; to grasp, to measure off
radicals.story: A hand 又 reaching down through the grass 艹 to snatch a bird 隹 — catching the quarry.
radicals.notes: Same phonetic as 獲 and 穫. Worded as an agent noun to stay clearly apart from 隺 'hooded hawk', the other one-off bird component in this batch.

radicals.meaning: insect, bug, worm; any small creeping creature
radicals.story: A coiled snake with its head raised — earliest writing used it for any small creeping thing, and it eventually settled on 'insect'.
radicals.notes: 虫 vs 中: 虫 is 中 with an extra horizontal through the base and a dot on the right. In 独 and 触 it marks a creature, not literally a bug.

radicals.meaning: clothing, garment, robe
radicals.story: A robe seen from the front: the top stroke is the collar and the strokes below are the crossed lapels falling open over two hanging sleeves.
radicals.variant_notes: 衤 is the compressed left-hand form (初裕複); 衣 is the standalone form and the bottom form (裂製).
radicals.notes: As the left-hand 衤 it is one stroke from 礻 (altar): 衤 has two ticks, 礻 has one.

radicals.meaning: clothing, garment (left-hand form)
radicals.story: 衣 (garment) squeezed into a narrow left-hand column, its collar hooked at the top and the hem splitting into two strokes at the bottom.
radicals.variant_notes: 衣 is the full form, used alone or stacked (裂, 製); 衤 is the compressed left-hand column (初, 裕, 複).
radicals.notes: The single most important discrimination in this list: count the bottom. 衤 (cloak, 5 strokes) has a stroke on EACH side of the stem; 礻 (altar, 4 strokes) has only ONE. 初 is cloth-and-scissors, 祝 is an altar — mixing them up flips the meaning entirely.

radicals.meaning: A long robe with a trailing hem.
radicals.story: A robe (衣) pulled open with 土 and 口 set into its middle — a long gown whose hem drags far behind.
radicals.notes: Named 'trailing gown' rather than 'robe' so it cannot collide with 衣. Used only in 遠 — a road as long as the trailing hem.

radicals.meaning: the legless top of 西, used as a flat lid over what follows
radicals.story: 西 'west' with its legs cut off, sitting like a flat lid on whatever comes below — treat it as a shape only, since inside 要 it is really a woman's hands on her hips and inside 価 it is the old cover 襾.
radicals.variant_notes: 襾 is the full Kangxi radical 'cover'; 西 is the everyday kanji 'west'; 覀 is the flattened form that caps another element.
radicals.notes: Only ever appears as a hat — you will never meet it standing alone.

radicals.meaning: to see, to look at
radicals.story: A big eye (目) set on a pair of walking legs (儿) — an eye out roaming and looking.
radicals.notes: 見 vs 貝: the eye of 見 is a clean 目 on legs; the shell 貝 has an extra crossbar inside and two small feet.

radicals.meaning: horn; angle, corner
radicals.story: An animal's horn drawn in profile: a tapering outline with the ridged growth-rings showing as the bars inside it.
radicals.notes: Not 用: 角 wears a slanted cap over the frame, 用 does not. In 解 the horn is being cut off a cow; in 触 it is a feeler making contact.

radicals.meaning: speech, saying, words — anything spoken or written down
radicals.story: A mouth 口 at the bottom with two lines of sound rising out of it, all under a lid 亠 — words leaving the lips.
radicals.notes: Almost always the left radical (ごんべん: 計, 記, 訪, 設). When it is on the right, it is the whole kanji 言 acting as a piece (信).

radicals.meaning: valley, ravine, gorge
radicals.story: A mouth (口) at the base with the strokes above splitting apart to either side — the opening of a ravine with the slopes parting over it.
radicals.notes: Sound carrier in 浴 ヨク, 欲 ヨク, 容 ヨウ, 裕 ユウ.

radicals.meaning: bean, pea; (originally) a stemmed ritual dish
radicals.story: A lidded bowl on a tall stem with a flared foot — originally a footed ritual serving dish, later borrowed outright to write 'bean', and the bowl still reads as a bean pot.
radicals.notes: The vessel origin is what explains 豊 (a dish heaped full = abundance) and 登 (raising the dish); 'bean' is the keyword because it is universal and 頭 'bean-head' is memorable.

radicals.meaning: pig, boar
radicals.story: A snouted head at the top, a fat body, trotters below and a curled tail flicking off to the right — a pig pictograph tipped upright.
radicals.notes: 家 'house' is a roof (宀) with a pig under it — the livestock lived indoors; 逐 'chase' is that pig bolting down the road (辶).

radicals.meaning: shell used as money; hence wealth, cost, payment, value
radicals.story: A ridged oval shell (the 目-shaped box) with two little feelers poking out below — a cowrie, which is what people spent before there were coins.
radicals.notes: Money is the point: 財, 貯, 買, 貸, 費, 資 all involve paying. 見 (see) has 儿 legs under the eye; 貝 has two short splayed strokes.

radicals.meaning: Coins threaded on a cord; to run right through.
radicals.story: A cord run straight through (毌) a cowrie shell (貝) — coins strung on a line.
radicals.notes: Used only in 慣 (the heart threaded through again and again — a habit).

radicals.meaning: blame, responsibility, demand payment
radicals.story: A thorn (the spiky top, originally 朿) pressed down onto a cowrie shell (貝) — leaning on someone hard for the money they owe.

radicals.meaning: precious, valuable, noble
radicals.story: A cowrie shell 貝 held up beneath what were once two hands — money raised high because it is treasure.
radicals.notes: Keyworded 'treasure' rather than the adjective 'precious' so it stays a picturable object; 貝 remains the plain cowrie shell.

radicals.meaning: run, hurry along
radicals.story: A runner leaning forward from the waist (the 土-shaped top) above a planted foot (龰), caught mid-stride.
radicals.notes: As a wrap-around radical (そうにょう) it runs down the left side and stretches along the bottom.

radicals.meaning: body, one's person, social station
radicals.story: A person drawn in profile with the belly bulging forward and a stroke slashed across it — the usual reading is a pregnant body, which is why the kanji means both 'body' and 'oneself'.
radicals.notes: Normally a left-hand radical (射・躍), but among these 811 it only ever appears as the whole character.

radicals.meaning: car, vehicle, cart
radicals.story: A wheeled cart seen from directly above — the axle runs top to bottom, the load-box sits in the middle, and the two crossbars are the wheels.
radicals.notes: 車 vs 東: the cart has one box on the axle, 東 (east) has the full tree 木 behind its box.

radicals.meaning: A body of troops; a military force.
radicals.story: War chariots (車) drawn up under a covering (冖) — wagons circled around the camp.
radicals.notes: Used only in 運 (an army on the road hauling its baggage — to carry, to transport).

radicals.meaning: spicy, pungent; bitter, harsh, painful
radicals.story: A broad handle (立) tapering down to one sharp point (十) — a branding needle, easiest to hold onto as the single sharp sting of a chili on the tongue.
radicals.notes: Exactly one stroke away from 幸 (happiness) — the classic mix-up, and a useful one (bitter vs lucky). Lends シン through 亲 into 新 and 親.

radicals.meaning: the fifth zodiac sign, the dragon; graphically a big bivalve shell
radicals.story: Traditionally the zodiac dragon, though the graph is usually traced to a big clam shell — the kind lashed to a stick as a field hoe, which is why 農 'farming' carries it — so read the strokes as a clawed shell sweeping out from under a cliff-like top.
radicals.notes: 振 'shake' is a hand plus 辰; the whole sound family (振, 震, 娠, 唇) is シン.

radicals.meaning: road, movement along a road; going, coming, advancing, retreating
radicals.story: A dot for a footfall above a stroke that drops down and then runs flat out to the right — a road unrolling beneath whatever it carries.
radicals.variant_notes: 辵 is the full ancient form (crossroads 彳 + foot 止); modern Japanese writes one dot (辶, 3 strokes) while older and Chinese fonts write two (⻍, 4 strokes).
radicals.notes: Wraps the bottom-left and is always written LAST. 廴 (as in 建, 延) is the same sweep without the dot on top.

radicals.meaning: A road, a way, a doctrine.
radicals.story: A head (首) travelling along the road radical (辶) — a person heading off down the main way.
radicals.notes: Keyed to 'highway' so it cannot collide with 辶, the road radical, which is one of its own parts. Used only in 導 (a thumb 寸 pointing the way down the highway — to guide).

radicals.meaning: a narrow-necked jar of fermented liquor
radicals.story: A big-bellied jar with a narrow neck and the liquor level ruled across inside — the vessel under every 'alcohol' character.
radicals.notes: 酒 'sake' adds water so you read it as the liquid; 配 'distribute' is someone crouching (己) to pour it out. Against 西: 酉 has the extra stroke ruled inside.

radicals.meaning: animal track; to distinguish one track from another
radicals.story: A splayed animal footprint pressed into the ground — a central pad-stroke with claw-flecks either side — which is why it came to mean telling one beast's track from another's.
radicals.notes: Not 米 'rice': 釆 adds a stroke on top and its flecks hang off the crossbar. 采 (pick) puts a claw 爫 above a tree instead.

radicals.meaning: To pick or gather by hand.
radicals.story: A downturned hand 爫 reaching into the branches of a tree 木 — plucking the fruit.
radicals.notes: Do not confuse with 釆 (Kangxi radical 165, 'distinguish'); 采 has the claw sitting on a tree.

radicals.meaning: village, hamlet; ri (old distance unit)
radicals.story: A rice paddy (田) resting on soil (土) — farmland plus ground to stand on is a village.
radicals.notes: Do NOT let the right-hand 阝 (city walls, from 邑) also take the word 'village' — 里 owns it here. In 黒 and 量 the 里 is a shape artifact rather than a real village.

radicals.meaning: heavy, weighty, piled in layers
radicals.story: A person bent forward over a fat bundle that is planted on the ground line at the bottom — a load too heavy to lift.

radicals.meaning: gold, metal, money; Friday
radicals.story: A roof of earth (土) with two nuggets tucked underneath — metal still sitting buried in the ground.
radicals.variant_notes: 釒 is the narrowed left-hand column form; in Japanese printing the left-side 金 keeps the same strokes but squeezes the base inward (鉄, 銀, 録).
radicals.notes: On the left it is the generic 'metal' marker, not specifically gold — 鉄 is iron, 銀 silver.

radicals.meaning: long; a senior, a chief
radicals.story: An old man with his uncut mane streaming down behind him — hair left long is the picture of length, and the elder wearing it is the chief.
radicals.notes: 帳 'curtain, ledger' is a long hanging cloth (巾); 張 'stretch' is a bow (弓) pulled long. Not the same as 彡, the three short hair-strokes.

radicals.meaning: gate, gateway, double doors
radicals.story: Two door-panels 戸 hung side by side under a single lintel — a double gate seen head-on.
radicals.notes: It wraps whatever stands in the gateway: sun 日 between the doors is 間 (interval), an ear 耳 at the gate is 聞 (hear), a mouth 口 at the gate is 問 (ask).

radicals.meaning: on the LEFT: a hill or embankment (阜). On the RIGHT: a walled village (邑)
radicals.story: A small hooked shape stacked on a vertical post, like steps cut into a slope — but read it as a HILL only when it stands on the left; on the right the identical glyph is a walled village.
radicals.variant_notes: Left-hand 阝 (こざとへん) is a squashed 阜 'hill' — 阻, 限, 降, 院. Right-hand 阝 (おおざと) is a squashed 邑 'village/city' — 郎, 部, 郵, 都. Identical strokes, unrelated primitives.
radicals.notes: IMPORTANT for mnemonic building: use 'hill' for left-position 阝 and 'village' for right-position 阝. Kangxi 170 (阜) on the left, 163 (邑) on the right.

radicals.meaning: a short-tailed bird
radicals.story: A short-tailed bird in profile — the top slash is its crest, the box its eye and folded wing, and the crossbars below its plumage and feet.
radicals.notes: Heisig calls this 'turkey'; it is really any short-tailed bird, as against the long-tailed 鳥. 集 is birds flocking onto a tree.

radicals.meaning: a bird held under a cover (its own sense is uncertain)
radicals.story: A short cover 冖 clamped down over a bird 隹 — the component's own origin is unclear, so read the shape plainly as a hawk wearing a falconer's hood.
radicals.notes: Shape-based keyword by design — no folk etymology invented. Deliberately worded to stay distinct from 蒦 'birdcatcher'.

radicals.meaning: A fat, choice bird; outstanding.
radicals.story: A short-tailed bird (隹) perched on 乃 — a fat, prize bird.
radicals.variant_notes: 攜 → 携 replaced 巂 with 隽.
radicals.notes: Used only in 携; it is the shinjitai stand-in for 巂 in 攜.

radicals.meaning: hire, employ, take someone on
radicals.story: A bird 隹 at the door 戸 — the migrating bird that shows up at the house each season, borrowed early on for taking someone on.
radicals.notes: One of the 811. 顧 is hire + head 頁: turning your head back to look over the people you took on.

radicals.meaning: rain
radicals.story: Drops falling from the sky: a flat heaven-line (一) over a cloud frame (冂) with four droplets hanging inside it.
radicals.variant_notes: ⻗ is the flattened roof form used when rain sits on top of another element (電, 雪, 雲, 需, 震); the standalone 雨 keeps the long hooked centre stroke.
radicals.notes: As a roof it marks weather kanji almost without exception.

radicals.meaning: cloud
radicals.story: Rain 雨 sitting over a curl of rising vapour 云 — the cloud the rain falls out of.
radicals.notes: In 曇 it is pure meaning: sun 日 with a cloud under it = overcast.

radicals.meaning: blue, green, fresh, young
radicals.story: A young plant sprouting (龶, from 生) above a mineral well (the bottom box, originally 丹) — the blue-green of fresh growth.
radicals.variant_notes: 靑 is the older printed form; its lower box is 円-like rather than 月. Same primitive.
radicals.notes: 青, 責 and 毒 all share the 龶 top; the bottoms (月 / 貝 / 毋) tell them apart.

radicals.meaning: wrong, not, un-; opposed, contrary
radicals.story: Two wings drawn back to back, three feathers each, beating away from one another — the picture of two things facing opposite ways.
radicals.notes: Means 'wrong / not' because the wings pull apart. Sits on top in 悲 (a heart with its wings torn in two = grief), on the right in 排・俳.

radicals.meaning: tanned leather; to go around, to deviate
radicals.story: Two feet (the upper and lower halves of 舛) circling in opposite directions around a walled hide (口) — the treading and turning that softens a raw skin into leather.
radicals.notes: Japanese stroke tables count this element as 10 (偉 12画, 違 13画, 衛 16画); Chinese/Kangxi tables give 9. In 偉 and 違 it carries only the sound イ. Distinct from 皮, the raw untanned skin.

radicals.meaning: sound, tone, noise
radicals.story: It began as 言 'words' with one extra stroke laid inside the mouth to mark a bare tone rather than speech; today read it as a figure standing (立) and letting a note ring out of a box (日).
radicals.notes: On top in 意, on the right in 暗. In 暗 it is the sound アン; in 意 it is the meaning — a sound rising in the heart.

radicals.meaning: head, face; the part of the body above the neck
radicals.story: A nose 自 under a single hairline stroke with two legs braced beneath — a person drawn with a head so big it fills the whole character.
radicals.notes: Always on the right: 順, 預, 領, 頭, 題, 額, 顔. Keep 頁 = 'head' and 首 = 'neck' strictly apart. Its bottom half looks like 貝 but the top is 一 + 自, not a shell.

radicals.meaning: A head cocked to one side; hence 'about, around' (ころ).
radicals.story: A head (頁) with a bent-over figure (匕) leaning into it — a head cocked to one side.
radicals.notes: Used only in 傾.

radicals.meaning: to fly, to leap, to skip over
radicals.story: Two wings, each ticked in with feathers, beating on either side of a body lifting upward — a bird just leaving the ground.
radicals.notes: Appears only as itself. Its left-right symmetry makes it easy to swap with 非 (split wings), which is also read ヒ.

radicals.meaning: food, eating; the left-hand form of 食
radicals.story: 食 squeezed for the left-hand slot — a lid (𠆢) over a bowl of cooked grain, with the bowl and its stand stacked below.
radicals.variant_notes: 食 is the standalone kanji and the whole/top form; 飠 is the compressed left-hand form used in 飯飲館; 𩙿 is the traditional printed left form.
radicals.notes: Never appears alone — it exists only as the left-hand squeeze of 食.

radicals.meaning: neck, head; chief, foremost
radicals.story: A face with a nose in it (自) wearing two tufts of hair on top (䒑) — a head drawn from the front, sitting on the neck that carries it.
radicals.notes: 首 was historically the sound element in 道, but the modern readings (シュ vs ドウ) no longer line up, so treat it as meaning only. 頁 is the other 'head' — keep 首 as the neck.

radicals.meaning: horse
radicals.story: A horse in profile: the mane bristling along the top, the body boxed in the middle, and the four legs and tail sweeping down into the four dots.
radicals.notes: The bottom 灬 here is legs and tail, not fire — the same four dots do mean fire in 熱 and 点.

radicals.meaning: bird
radicals.story: A crested head on top, a folded wing down the middle and four dots for tail and claws — a bird in profile, and removing the eye stroke gives 烏, the crow too black to show its eye.
radicals.notes: The long-tailed bird. Keep it apart from 隹, the stubby short-tailed bird that heads 集・雑・難・推.
