radicals.meaning: hemp, flax; (by extension) numbness
radicals.story: Two hemp plants (林) hung up to dry under the roof of an open-sided shed (广) — a drying house full of hemp fiber.
radicals.notes: A very reliable マ sound: 摩・磨・魔 all follow it.

radicals.meaning: the colour yellow
radicals.story: A 龷 crown over 由 with two legs 八 beneath — the graphic origin is disputed, so take the fixed shape as given and call it yellow.
radicals.notes: Kangxi radical 201, but not one of the 811 study kanji; in 横 it is purely the オウ sound.

radicals.meaning: a foot in motion — the flattened bottom-of-character form of 止
radicals.story: 止 'footprint' squashed flat and planted at the bottom of a character, a foot caught mid-stride — it holds up both 走 'run' and 足 'leg'.
radicals.variant_notes: 止 is the free-standing form and the top/left form; 龰 is the flattened form that sits underneath.
radicals.notes: 走 is soil + striding foot (kicking up dirt); 足 is a mouth-shaped kneecap over the same foot.

radicals.meaning: no independent meaning; the hooked マ-shaped stroke pair on top of 予 and 矛
radicals.story: A bent stroke with a tick tucked under it — the shape of katakana マ, best pictured as the barbed point of a spear.
radicals.notes: Pairs with 𠄐 to build 予 and 矛; 厶 is the closed triangle version and is easy to mix up with it.

radicals.meaning: three bars on an upright; no independent meaning
radicals.story: Three horizontal bars skewered by a single upright, like a low garden trellis — in 青 and 毒 it is a flattened 生 (growing plant), elsewhere it is only this shape.
radicals.notes: Never written alone. It converges from several different sources (生 in 青/毒, 毛 in 表, 堇 in 勤), so do not attach a meaning to it.

radicals.meaning: two posts through a rail; no independent meaning
radicals.story: Two short posts driven through a horizontal rail, like a low hurdle — in 共 it caps the pair of raised hands (八) below.
radicals.notes: Never written alone. Distinguish from 艹 (flowers), whose two uprights are short slants sitting ON the bar, and from 廿 (twenty), whose uprights hang below it.

radicals.meaning: Two hands working at something spread out below them.
radicals.story: Beneath the splayed top strokes sit two hands 廾, pressing and rolling — the same top block that 巻 and 勝 wear.

radicals.meaning: a hand; the two-stroke hand that tops 友, 右, 左, 有 and 布
radicals.story: A slash with a bar laid across it — the outline of a hand seen from the wrist, the same hand as 又 tilted the other way.
radicals.notes: Genuinely a hand: 友 is two hands clasped, 右 is a hand at the mouth, 有 is a hand holding meat 月.

radicals.meaning: a slash crossed by a short bar; a recurring top-shape with no meaning of its own
radicals.story: A short slash pierced by a horizontal bar — a hairpin pushed through a topknot, though it is really only a shape: a pestle in 午 and the head of a fluttering banner in 旅 and 族.
radicals.notes: The hairpin image comes from 毎/海, where this really was a woman with a hair ornament.

radicals.meaning: a slash capped by a downward hook; a recurring top-shape with no meaning of its own
radicals.story: A short slash finished with a hook curling down, like a hooked beak angled over whatever sits beneath it — honestly just a recurring shape, since it descends from a hand in 争, a bent-over person in 色 and 負, and a fish's head in 魚.
radicals.notes: Distinct from 爫 (claw), which has three ticks under its bar.

radicals.meaning: no independent meaning; a merged shape that is an ox in 告 and a footprint in 先
radicals.story: A horn slanting off a crossbar with a post below — the head of an ox squeezed under whatever sits on it, though in 先 the identical shape came from a footprint instead.
radicals.notes: It is 牛 with the vertical stopped short; two unrelated ancestors collapsed into one modern shape.

radicals.meaning: a heaped mound of earth; the rise an army camps on
radicals.story: A heap of earth drawn in stacked layers with a slant flying off the top — the small hill an army pitches camp on.
radicals.notes: 師 'master, commander' is the officer on the mound before his banner; 追 'pursue' chases him down the road. Related in sense to 阝 (hill) but a separate shape.

radicals.meaning: no independent meaning; one stroke that drops and squares off to the right
radicals.story: Not a picture of anything — a single stroke that comes down and turns a right angle to the right, exactly like a metal L-bracket propping up whatever sits on it.
radicals.notes: Some charts file it under radical 5 (乙) alongside 乚 and 乛; treat it as a stroke, not a meaning.

radicals.meaning: a single stroke that runs right then turns sharply down; no meaning of its own
radicals.story: One stroke that runs to the right and then breaks sharply downward — the corner of a bent arm, an elbow.
radicals.notes: Pure stroke-shape. It is the frame of 力, 万, 方, 司, 成, 別 and 局 — never carries meaning.

radicals.meaning: What survives of 殸, a stone chime slung on a frame.
radicals.story: A hooked bracket with a flat slab caught inside it — a chime stone hung from its rack, waiting to be struck.
radicals.notes: 声 comes from 聲 = 殸 (struck chime) + 耳 (ear), so the chime reading is the real source of the 'sound' sense.

radicals.meaning: a single stroke: a vertical that bends away at the foot
radicals.story: A single stroke drawn straight down and then flicked aside at the foot, like a nail whose tip has been bent over — a stroke, not a meaning.
radicals.notes: It is the central downstroke in the lower half of 長 and 展; 乚 turns the other way and 亅 hooks upward.

radicals.meaning: no independent meaning; the hooked lower half of 予 and 矛
radicals.story: A stroke that runs to the right, drops straight down and flicks up at the tip — a hook left dangling from a beam.

radicals.meaning: A collar bar with two folded marks under it.
radicals.story: A lid stroke 亠 with two small figures tucked beneath it — read it as the collar and lapels of the marked jacket that 卒 once pictured.

radicals.meaning: A hood with a beam laid across inside it.
radicals.story: The wide hood 冂 with a single horizontal spanning it wall to wall, like the beam over a doorway.

radicals.meaning: A frame with four drops falling inside it.
radicals.story: A hood 冂 split by an upright with two drops on each side — rain seen through a window frame.

radicals.meaning: An earthen pot; the shinjitai stand-in for 缶.
radicals.story: The lower block of 揺's right side is an open-topped box (凵) with a shaft (干) standing in it — this is the flattened form of 缶, an earthen jar, so picture a fat clay pot.
radicals.variant_notes: Stands in for 缶 inside the 䍃 element of 揺・謡・遥.
radicals.notes: Distinct from 酉, the wine jug. Used only in 揺.

radicals.meaning: The sun coming up through tall grass.
radicals.story: A sun (日) wedged between two 十 strokes that were once tufts of tall grass — the sun rising through the reeds.
radicals.notes: Used only in 朝 (the sun already up while the moon 月 still hangs — morning).

radicals.meaning: A baby drawn head-downward at the moment of birth.
radicals.story: It is the child 子 flipped upside down — head first, arms trailing behind.

radicals.meaning: A kneeling person held down by a hand.
radicals.story: A hand 又 clamped onto the shoulder of a kneeling figure 卩 — a prisoner held fast.
radicals.notes: 報 pairs it with handcuffs 幸: the sentence passed on a captive is the news that gets reported.

radicals.meaning: A hand pushing a broom; to advance bit by bit.
radicals.story: A stubby broom (帚 with its handle clipped off) gripped in a hand (又) — sweeping.
radicals.notes: Two words so it cannot collide with 帚 (broom) or 又 alone. Used only in 寝.

radicals.meaning: A mouth with a lid laid over it.
radicals.story: A short horizontal sits flat on top of a mouth 口 like a lid on a jar; it fills the crook of 司.

radicals.meaning: three cut stalks bound together by a crossing tie
radicals.story: Three stalks (三) bound by a crossing tie (人) into a sheaf of cut grain, sprouting over the sun in 春 and stored under a roof in 実.
radicals.notes: The same cap tops 奉, 秦 and 泰 — only what sits below tells those four apart.

radicals.meaning: Bundles of straw stuffed in as insulation.
radicals.story: Under a roof 宀, bundles of straw packed tight around the person sheltering inside.
radicals.notes: 寒 completes the picture with two ice strokes ⺀ underneath — straw packed in against the freeze.

radicals.meaning: the pole 干 with two ticks cut into its head; no meaning of its own
radicals.story: The forked pole 干 with two ticks cut into its head — exactly the block sitting inside 南 and under the 土 of 幸, and it means nothing on its own.
radicals.notes: In 幸 it is the lower half of the manacles; in 南 it is the innards of a hanging bell — different origins, same printed block.

radicals.meaning: A stand for holding something up; the 畀 element, 'to give'.
radicals.story: A boxy 田 set on a two-legged plinth (丌) — a small stand for lifting something up to present it.
radicals.variant_notes: Written 畀 outside the 鼻 glyph.
radicals.notes: Used only in 鼻, where it sits under 自 (the nose pictograph) purely as a sound-marker.

radicals.meaning: a stake with cord wound down it in even, ordered turns
radicals.story: A post with a cord wound down it in even turns, a job that has to be done in strict order — which is why it carries 弟 'younger brother, next in line' and 第 'sequence number'.
radicals.notes: Add the two ticks 丷 on top and you have 弟 itself; put 竹 on top instead and you have 第.

radicals.meaning: No independent meaning — the whole right-hand block of 微.
radicals.story: A flattened 山 stacked on a pair of legs with 攵 (a hand and stick) alongside; it carries no independent sense, so simply see a tiny peak being tapped.
radicals.variant_notes: Often written 𡵂 + 攵 as two separate pieces.
radicals.notes: The etymology of 微 is disputed; describing the shape is the honest option. Used only in 微.

radicals.meaning: water surging upward (the right half of 滕)
radicals.story: Two hands 龹 flinging water 氺 upward — water bursting out in a gusher.
radicals.notes: The トウ phonetic shared by 藤, 騰 and 滕. Written almost identically to 泰; distinct keyword avoids any clash with 水/氵.

radicals.meaning: A whorl with thread wound onto it.
radicals.story: A rounded head sitting on a shaft with a bar driven through it — the spinning whorl that also tops 恵 and 穂.

radicals.meaning: A foot planted flat on a line so it cannot move.
radicals.story: The foot 止 with a bar drawn beneath it, pinning it in place — the squared-off form used at the bottom of 定.

radicals.meaning: sheep; the top form of 羊
radicals.story: The head of the sheep 羊 with its horns curling down, flattened so it can perch on top of whatever follows.
radicals.variant_notes: 羊 is the full form, standing alone or sitting on the right/bottom (洋, 遅); 𦍌 (also printed ⺷) is the top form in 美, 着, 差, 義 and 様, where the sheep's bottom stroke is absorbed into the element below.
radicals.notes: 美 really is 'big sheep' — a fat sheep was beautiful.

radicals.meaning: A newborn sheep.
radicals.story: 土 sitting on a clipped 羊 (sheep) — the older form wrote 大 over 羊, a big sheep's newborn, so see a lamb standing on bare ground.
radicals.variant_notes: Shinjitai form of 羍; the top 大 has been rewritten as 土.
radicals.notes: Deliberately 'lamb' not 'sheep', so it cannot collide with 羊 or 𦍌. Used only in 達.

radicals.meaning: A hand gripping a writing brush (the clipped top of 聿).
radicals.story: A fist closed around an upright brush, with the brush's long bottom stroke left off so the 日 below can slot under it.
radicals.variant_notes: Same hand-and-brush as 聿; here it is trimmed of its final stroke, which 書's bottom half completes.

radicals.meaning: The head, drawn as a face seen head-on.
radicals.story: A nose 自 with a brow line drawn across the top of it — a bare head, the same head that 頁 and 首 are built on.
radicals.notes: Keep it distinct from 頁: 頁 is the head with legs beneath it, 𦣻 is the head alone.

radicals.meaning: two hands reaching in from either side to raise something
radicals.story: One hand curling in from the left and another from the right, hooking under whatever sits between them to hoist it up.
radicals.notes: Kept as 'lifting hands' to stay distinct from 廾 (the two hands at the bottom of a character) and from 臼 'mortar', which it is drawn almost identically to.

radicals.meaning: (shape) a figure with arms outstretched; the sound element of 漢 and 難
radicals.story: The oldest form is usually read as a person held over a drought-ritual fire, but as written today it stacks a flat straw hat (廿) on a mouth (口) on a pair of outstretched arms (夫) — a scarecrow, which is what the shape honestly looks like.
radicals.variant_notes: 堇 (in 勤, 謹, 僅) is the closely related cousin: it ends in 土 where 𦰩 ends in the 大-like outstretched arms. Learn them as a pair, not as one shape.
radicals.notes: Counted as 10 strokes in the Japanese forms (漢 13画, 難 18画).

radicals.meaning: A hard-shelled grain bug.
radicals.story: A small hook 厶 riding on an insect 虫 — read it as the tough grain weevil.
radicals.notes: 強 originally named a hard-shelled insect and only later came to mean 'strong'; this element is the bug, with 弓 on the left supplying the rest of the old shape.

radicals.meaning: The lower, hanging half of a robe 衣.
radicals.story: Take the garment 衣 and strip off its collar 亠 — what is left is the skirt falling in folds.

radicals.meaning: The rump and legs of a four-legged animal.
radicals.story: The bottom block of 象 and of 豕 (pig) — the sweep of the back with four short legs dropping off it, so just see trotters.
radicals.notes: Like 𫩏, an arbitrary slice of the 象 pictograph, though it is genuinely the animal-leg portion shared with 豕. Used only in 象.

radicals.meaning: foot, leg (left-hand form of 足)
radicals.story: A kneecap or ankle joint (口) planted on the foot below it, heel and toes splayed out — the whole leg from knee to sole.
radicals.variant_notes: 足 is the full character, used standalone and when the element sits right or bottom; 𧾷 is the same foot squeezed narrow for the left column, its final stroke tucked in instead of sweeping out (路, 躍, 跡, 踊).
radicals.notes: Any kanji with 𧾷 on the left is about feet, walking, jumping or roads.

radicals.meaning: A Z-bend resting on a baseline.
radicals.story: The stroke doubles back on itself and lands on a flat foot — a zigzag, which is exactly 五 with its lid stroke taken off.

radicals.meaning: No independent meaning — a box with one stroke through it.
radicals.story: The middle band of 象: a box (囗) with a single stroke barred through it, an arbitrary slice of the elephant's body.
radicals.notes: 象 is a single whole-body elephant pictograph; the IDS database slices it into three pieces that never had meanings of their own. Used only in 象.

radicals.meaning: Vapour rising out of a window — the picture behind 尚.
radicals.story: Two strokes puffing upward out of a small window — smoke escaping through the roof vent.
radicals.variant_notes: This is the 尚 element as it is written on top of 常; 尚 itself never appears alone among these 811 kanji.

radicals.meaning: three short upward strokes; no independent meaning
radicals.story: Three short strokes flicking upward like sparks thrown off a fire — modern print merged several unrelated older tops (the crossed sticks of 學, the flames of 勞) into this one shape, so read it as shape only.
radicals.notes: Always the cap of a character, almost always sitting directly on 冖: 学, 労, 覚. Do not read meaning into it — it is a post-war simplification.

radicals.meaning: the crested heron 雚, reduced to its shinjitai shape
radicals.story: The squeezed-down modern form of 雚: a few quick strokes for the crest sitting over a bird 隹, a long-necked stork.
radicals.notes: The same reduced element appears in 勧 and 歓; 観 is the stork's fixed stare plus 見 'see'.
